title: Switch from eculizumab to satralizumab in aquaporin 4 immunoglobulin G–seropositive neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder: a case series report
creator: Hesham Abboud, Adnan Subei, Buse Sengul, Robert K. Shin, Paige Goulette, Rosemarie Walch, Jeanie Coté, Robert Pace, Ahmed Z. Obeidat, Lisa Ferayorni, Shervin Gholizadeh
description: ObjectivesThis case series describes adults with aquaporin 4 immunoglobulin G–seropositive (AQP4-IgG+) neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder (NMOSD) who switched treatment from eculizumab to satralizumab.MethodsCase information for patients with AQP4-IgG+ NMOSD who received satralizumab for ≥6 months was obtained from US healthcare providers from April 2022 to January 2024.

title: Graph attention network‐driven single‐cell omics analysis reveals how B4GALNT1‐mediated glycosylation remodelling of the ferroptosis–pyroptosis network promotes drug resistance in hepatocellular carcinoma
creator: Lihan Bie, Biao Xu, Haitao Shen, Shuwen Ren, Xiaoyang Yao, Zhouhong Xiang, Zheng Xu
description: BackgroundAcquired resistance to sorafenib in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is accompanied by coordinated changes in oxidative‐stress handling and regulated cell‐death pathways, yet how membrane organisation connects these adaptations is not fully resolved. We therefore examined whether B4GALNT1, a ganglioside biosynthetic glycosyltransferase, couples changes in ganglioside composition and lipid‐raft architecture to ferroptosis regulation and caspase‐1/GSDMD‐associated signalling in sorafenib‐resistant HCC.

title: CD56neg CD16+ cells represent a distinct mature NK cell subset with altered phenotype and are associated with adverse clinical outcome upon expansion in AML
creator: Julia Wlosik, Florence Orlanducci, Manon Richaud, Clemence Demerle, Amira Ben Amara, Marie-Sarah Rouviere, Philippe Livrati, Laurent Gorvel, Marie-Anne Hospital, Nicolas Dulphy, Raynier Devillier, Norbert Vey, Daniel Olive, Anne-Sophie Chretien
description: IntroductionAcute myeloid leukemia (AML) is a rare haematological cancer with poor 5-years overall survival (OS) and high relapse rate. Leukemic cells are sensitive to Natural Killer (NK) cell mediated killing. However, NK cells are highly impaired in AML, which promote AML immune escape from NK cell immune surveillance.

title: Experimental manipulation of ecological constraints influences conflict but not cooperation in the humbug damselfish Dascyllus aruanus
creator: Rebecca Branconi, Marian Y L Wong, Daniel B Stouffer, Theresa Rueger, Peter Buston
description: Animal societies vary widely in levels of cooperation and conflict, and understanding the causes of this variation is a central goal in evolutionary biology. As with other features of animal societies, relatedness, competitiveness and ecological constraints (e.g. habitat saturation and risks of dispersal) have been proposed as key factors explaining variation in cooperation and conflict.

title: A case of pulmonary ALK-positive histiocytosis combined with Birt-Hogg-Dubé syndrome carrying an EML4::ALK gene fusion: a case report and literature review
creator: Shuzhe Yang, Zhongyuan Bai, Qi Zhao, Yajing Wang, Yanfeng Xi
description: In this article, we report the first case of a 61-year-old woman who was diagnosed with both nodules and cystic lesions in her lungs. The lung nodules were diagnosed as ALK-positive histiocytosis (APH) carrying an EML4::ALK gene fusion, which microscopically displayed a mixed morphology of foamy cells, spindle cells, and Touton’s giant cells.

title: A cross-sectional study on the moderating effect of self-efficacy on the relationship between sociodemographic variables and nutrition literacy among older adults in rural areas of North Sichuan
creator: Shasha Liu, Xiaomei Fan, Li Jiang, Tao Liu
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). ObjectiveThe purpose of this study is to examine the moderating role of self-efficacy among rural elderly individuals in northern Sichuan Province in the relationship between certain sociodemographic variables and nutritional literacy.MethodsConvenience sampling was used to select 264 elderly individuals aged 60 and above from rural communities in Cangxi County, Guangyuan City, Yilong County, Nanchong City, and Bazhou District, Bazhong City, Sichuan Province.

title: Self-organized spectral adjustment in echolocation sounds within group-flying bats
creator: Kazuma Hase, Tasuku Miyazaki, Seiya Oka, Noriyoshi Senoo, Hiraku Nishimori, Masashi Shiraishi, Ken Yoda, Kohta I. Kobayasi, Shizuko Hiryu
description: Self-organized behaviour has been extensively studied in group dynamics in animals, with a strong focus on movement coordination in species like fish and birds. By contrast, far less attention has been paid to vocal interactions within animal groups. Here, we unveil a self-organized vocal behaviour in echolocating bats (Miniopterus fuliginosus), characterized by their adaptive responses to jamming stimuli.

title: Developing and demonstrating an atomistic and holistic model of anthropometric failure among children under five years of age using the National Family Health Survey (NFHS)-5 data from India
creator: E. R. Nandeep, Abdul Jaleel, P. Bhaskar Reddy, J. J. Babu Geddam, Samarasimha N. Reddy, Rajkumar Hemalatha
description: IntroductionComposite Index of Anthropometric Failure (CIAF) and its further modifications have not incorporated all the combinations of malnutrition. We propose a new model incorporating all the forms of malnutrition among children under five years of age. However, the current models might misclassify a growing child as malnourished.

title: Development of right ventricular electromechanical dyssynchrony following surgical repair of tetralogy of Fallot in infants
creator: Andrew W. McCrary, Sydney D. Collins, Zebulon Z. Spector, P. Andrea Kropf, Piers C. A. Barker, Joseph Kisslo, Daniel E. Forsha
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundIn adolescents and adults with tetralogy of Fallot (TOF), right ventricle (RV) electromechanical dyssynchrony (EMD) due to right bundle branch block (RBBB) is associated with reduced exercise capacity and RV dysfunction. While the development of RBBB following surgical repair of tetralogy of Fallot (rTOF) is a frequent sequela, it is not known whether EMD is present in every patient immediately following rTOF.

title: Evidence for cortisol production in a shark
creator: Alyssa M Weinrauch, Ian A Bouyoucos, W Gary Anderson
description: Corticosteroids are essential regulators of numerous physiological functions in vertebrates, including energy balance, immune responses, osmotic balance and metabolism. The terminal corticosteroids are highly conserved across jawed vertebrates, where cortisol or corticosterone mediates these physiological responses. Elasmobranchs, however, have a unique dominant circulating steroid, 1⍺-hydroxycorticosterone, and since its discovery it has been presumed that elasmobranchs do not produce cortisol.

title: Mathematical simulations of paediatric haemodynamics in isolated ventricular septal defect
creator: Mitchel J. Colebank, Alfonso Limon, Anthony Chang, Brandon Wong, Wyman Lai, Hamilton Baker
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Computer modelling of the cardiovascular system has the potential to revolutionize personalized medical care. This is especially promising for congenital heart defects, such as ventricular septal defect (VSD), a hole between the two ventricles of the heart. However, relatively few studies have built computer models for VSD, nor have they considered how natural adaptation to the cardiovascular system with age might interact with the presence of a small-, medium- or large-sized VSD.

title: Analysis of Vaccenic and Elaidic acid in foods using a silver ion cartridge applied to GC × GC-TOFMS
creator: Miyoung Yoo, Hyun Jeong Lee, Kwang-Won Lee, Dongwon Seo
description: BackgroundTrans fatty acids (TFAs) are unsaturated fatty acids, with vaccenic acid (VA) and elaidic acid (EA) being the major constituents. While VA has been associated with beneficial effects on health and anti-cancer properties, EA is found in hardened vegetable oils and is linked to an increased risk of cardiovascular diseases.

title: The relationship between psychological abuse, athlete satisfaction, eating disorder and self-harm indicators in elite athletes
creator: Erin Willson, Stephanie Buono, Gretchen Kerr, Ashley Stirling
description: IntroductionPsychological abuse continues to be the most frequently reported type of maltreatment among athletes leading to negative mental health such as low mood and self-esteem, increased anxiety, self-harm, and eating disorders. Preliminary evidence suggests athlete satisfaction can influence the perceived outcomes associated with psychological abuse.

title: Personalized haemodynamic modelling for non-invasive quantification of arterial stiffness in the human vasculature
creator: Xiangdong Zhang, Dan Wu, Fen Miao, Jiajie Zhong, Fan Yu, Xuejiao Zhang, Hao Liu, Ye Li
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Arterial stiffness is a pivotal predictor of cardiovascular events, yet its in vivo characterization remains elusive because arterial wall mechanics cannot be directly measured. Conventional inverse approaches require high-resolution imaging to resolve wall motion, restricting their clinical applicability. Here, we present a non-invasive computational framework that infers regional arterial stiffness solely from routinely acquired pressure and blood flow velocity waveforms by leveraging personalized one-dimensional haemodynamic models of the human arterial network.

title: Early-life cortisol exposure modulates habituation to human disturbance in fallow deer fawns
creator: George B. Brown, Dómhnall J. Jennings
description: The survival of vulnerable juveniles depends on how they respond to threat, yet the escape behaviour of individuals often differs despite similar exposure to stimuli. These differences may arise from interactions between experience, early-life physiology and developing behaviours such as play.

title: Nanogenerators for gas sensing applications
creator: Ye-Xuan Zhen, Gong Wang, Yun-Fei Li, Yu Yu
description: Gas sensors are now widely employed in many industries due to the rapid speed of industrialization and the growth of the Internet of Things. However, the wearability and mobility of traditional gas sensors are limited by their high reliance on external power sources.

title: Ploidy is associated with multielemental reorganization across soft and mineralized body compartments
creator: Punidan Jeyasingh, Marissa Roseman, Josh Bliss, Yetkin Ipek, Maurine Neiman
description: Polyploidy alters nuclear DNA content, gene dosage and cellular organization, but its consequences for organismal chemistry remain poorly resolved, particularly in animals. Because nucleic acids and associated cellular machinery require coordinated allocation of multiple elements, ploidy-associated differences may extend beyond the well-established consequences for body phosphorus content to broader multielemental organization.

title: Neural correlates of thermal stimulation during active touch
creator: Wanjoo Park, Georgios Korres, Muhammad Hassan Jamil, Mohamad Eid
description: IntroductionThermal feedback technologies have been explored in human-computer interaction to provide secondary information and enhance the overall user experience. Unlike fast-response haptic modalities such as vibration and force feedback, the human brain's processes associated with thermal feedback are not fully understood.

title: The association of visceral fat metabolism score with hyperuricemia—evidence from NHANES 1999–2018
creator: Lin Xie, Huali Qu, Dandan Lai, Juan Li, Xushan Chen, Jiajia Xie
description: ObjectivesDespite substantial evidence that visceral obesity is an epidemiological risk factor for hyperuricemia (HUA), studies on the connection between the Metabolic Score for Visceral Fat (METS-VF) and HUA remain insufficient. This research focused on METS-VF’s potential role as a risk factor for HUA.

title: CATCHing chronic GVHD
creator: Matthias Fante, Daniel Wolff
description: to establish a foundation for future trials investigating preemptive interventions for incipient and subclinical cGVHD and organ-specific biomarker studies. This prospective, longitudinal observational study systematically describes the clinical course of 208 patients from before alloHSCT through the first 12 months after alloHSCT enrolled at 7 US centers between November 2019 and April 2024.

title: New insights in animal models of neurotoxicity-induced neurodegeneration
creator: Coral Sanfeliu, Clara Bartra, Cristina Suñol, Eduard Rodríguez-Farré
description: The high prevalence of neurodegenerative diseases is an unintended consequence of the high longevity of the population, together with the lack of effective preventive and therapeutic options. There is great pressure on preclinical research, and both old and new models of neurodegenerative diseases are required to increase the pipeline of new drugs for clinical testing.

title: Effects of the tobacco–maize relay intercropping pattern on soil nutrients and soil microbial diversity
creator: Kang Yang, Shuhui Zi, Chengren Ouyang
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). The imbalanced soil nutrient status caused by the long-term monoculture of flue-cured tobacco are a concern. The tobacco–maize relay intercropping, widely used in Yunnan, may improve soil nutrients by enhancing the soil microbial community, but this remains unexplored. This study employed high-throughput sequencing technology to examine soil microbial diversity under tobacco monoculture and tobacco–maize relay intercropping, using the varieties Hongda and K326, respectively.

title: Preventive governance for patient‐centred medical AI
creator: Linghua Yu
description: ngful human oversight, patient autonomy and health equity. 1 , 2 , 3 Recent work on AI‐driven clinical consultations and autonomous agents indicates that these questions have shifted from hypothetical scenarios to emerging clinical realities. 4 , 5 One question threads through these discussions: what happens when something goes wrong?

title: Transdermal electrophysiological recordings of diet-induced small fiber peripheral neuropathy using a needle electrode array in mice and man
creator: Magdalena Blaszkiewicz, Lydia Caron, Brooke Villinski, Joshua Passarelli, Julia M. Towne, Naeemah M. Story, Erin Merchant, Furrukh S. Khan, Nuri Emanetoglu, Leonard Kass, Rosemary L. Smith, Kristy L. Townsend
description: BackgroundDiabetic peripheral neuropathy (DPN) is a common complication of diabetes. Proactive treatment options remain limited, which is exacerbated by a lack of sensitive and convenient diagnostics, especially early in disease progression or specifically to assess small fiber neuropathy (SFN), the loss of distal small diameter axons that innervate tissues and organs.

title: The effect of deep magnetic stimulation on the cardiac-brain axis post-sleep deprivation: a pilot study
creator: Qiongfang Cao, Peng Zhang, Fangfang Liu, Mengyan Jin, Yuhan Wang, Hanrui Zeng, Xiechuan Weng, Fan Xu
description: IntroductionSleep deprivation (SD) significantly disrupts the homeostasis of the cardiac-brain axis, yet the neuromodulation effects of deep magnetic stimulation (DMS), a non-invasive and safe method, remain poorly understood.MethodsSixty healthy adult males were recruited for a 36-h SD study, they were assigned to the DMS group or the control group according to their individual willing.

title: Enhanced sonocatalytic degradation of diethylstilbestrol using multi-walled carbon nanotubes under ultrasonic irradiation☆
creator: Manman Sun, Yihan Sun, Jingzhen Wang, Shengkun Tang, Hongyu Chen
description: The continuous release of endocrine-disrupting compounds (EDCs) into Aquatic habitats have emerged as a considerable environmental issue due to their persistence, propensity for bioaccumulation, and detrimental biological consequences, even at low concentrations. Among these contaminants, diethylstilbestrol (DES), a synthetic estrogen, has attracted considerable attention because of its strong endocrine-disrupting activity and resistance to conventional wastewater treatment technologies.

title: Physicochemical properties and molecular mechanisms of different resistant starch subtypes in rice
creator: Cheng Liang, Haoyang Xu, Hui You, Ouling Zhang, Yiman Han, Qingyu Li, Yungao Hu, Xunchao Xiang
description: Resistant starch (RS) can help prevent diabetes and decrease calorie intake and that from plants are the main source of mankind consumption. Rice is many people’s staple food and that with higher RS will help health management. A significantly positive correlation exists between apparent amylose content (AAC) of rice and its RS content.

title: Diversity and divergence of two sympatric, sibling octopus species
creator: Gabrielle C Coffing, Silas Tittes, Scott T Small, Andrew D Kern
description: Coleoid cephalopods have convergently evolved many traits shared with vertebrates, including camera-type eyes, large brain-to-body size ratios, and complex behaviors. Most evolutionary studies of cephalopods have compared individual genomes of taxa that diverged tens to hundreds of millions of years ago; yet, very few have examined more recent evolution from a population genetics perspective.

title: Special issue of Medicinal Chemistry Research in honor of Dr. Kenneth A. Jacobson
creator: Carola Gallo-Rodriguez, Juan Bautista Rodriguez, Pnina Fishman
description: gnized for his transformative contributions to medicinal chemistry in deeply comprehending purinergic receptor chemistry and translational drug discovery. Dr. Kenneth Jacobson received a B.A. from Reed College in 1975, followed by an M.S. in 1978 and a Ph.D. under Prof. Murray Goodman’s supervision in 1981 from the University of California, San Diego.

title: Transcriptomic landscape of staminate catkins development during overwintering process in Betula platyphylla
creator: Jingyun Zhang, Jiayuan Shi, Kehao Zeng, Mengjie Cai, Xingguo Lan
description: Betula platyphylla, belonging to the cold-specialized lineage Betulaceae, exhibits a unique reproductive strategy where staminate catkins emerge in the first summer and undergo an overwintering process, culminating in flowering in the following year. However, the underlying regulatory mechanism remains unclear. In this study, we investigated the male germline development of B. platyphylla in four distinct stages: microsporocytes in Oct.

title: Preliminary Investigations into the Possibility of Using Hot Torsion Testing to Model Microstructural Evolution During Aluminum Extrusion
creator: Piotr Korczak, Konrad Błażej Laber, Sonia Boczkal, Dariusz Leśniak, Krzysztof Remsak
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). This paper outlines preliminary findings from studies on the possibility of using hot torsion testing for the physical modeling of microstructural evolution during aluminum alloy extrusion processes. Accordingly, two plastic deformation processes were investigated: high-temperature torsion and extrusion. The studies were conducted within the temperature range characteristic of the extrusion of 16 mm diameter round profiles made of EN AW-6060 aluminum alloy, with different cooling rates after deformation.

title: Plant growth–promoting rhizobacteria: Peribacillus frigoritolerans 2RO30 and Pseudomonas sivasensis 2RO45 for their effect on canola growth under controlled as well as natural conditions
creator: Joanna Świątczak, Agnieszka Kalwasińska, Maria Swiontek Brzezinska
description: Even though canola is one of the most important industrial crops worldwide, it has high nutrient requirements and is susceptible to pests and diseases. Therefore, natural methods are sought to support the development of these plants. One of those methods could be a plant growth–promoting rhizobacteria (PGPR) that have a beneficial effect on plant development.

title: Menopause Education in Obstetrics and Gynecology Residency Training: A Scoping Review
creator: Haggar Zoe Aspitz Leibou, Adriane Burgess, Josselyn Thornton, Melissa Noel, Carie Burke
description: Obstetrics and gynecology residents' knowledge of and comfort with menopause is limited despite the Council on Resident Education in Obstetrics and Gynecology objectives of menopause training in residency. Menopause affects more than 1 billion women worldwide, yet the medical community has not consistently met the complex physical, psychological, and social needs associated with the menopause transition.

title: Fast-Acting Subperception Spinal Cord Stimulation for Persistent Spinal Pain Syndromes: Real-World Outcomes for up to 3 Years in an “As-Treated” Cohort from a Global Observational Study
creator: Clark Metzger, Blake Hammond, Richard Ferro, Jose Paz-Solis, Georgios Kyriakopoulos, Philippe Rigoard, Ashish Gulve, Jose Emilio Llopis, Pablo Andrade, Sarah Love-Jones, Jan Willem Kallewaard, Jan Vesper, Stephen Pyles, Simon Bayerl
description: Background/Objectives: Evidence on the effectiveness of spinal cord stimulation using fast-acting subperception therapy (FAST-SCS) in patients with persistent spinal pain syndrome (PSPS) remains limited. We evaluated clinical outcomes of FAST-SCS in patients with PSPS types 1 (i.e., non-surgical back pain) and 2 (i.e., failed back surgery syndrome).

title: Mental Health Indicators in Older Men Practising Aquatic Exercise and Multicomponent Exercise: An Exploratory Cross-Sectional Study
creator: Carlos Farinha, José Pedro Ferreira, Ana Teixeira, Samuel Honório, Marco Batista, Jorge Santos, Miguel Rebelo, João Petrica, João Serrano
description: Background/Objectives: Regular physical exercise is considered a relevant strategy for promoting physical and mental health in older adults. However, studies using exclusively male samples that directly compare different exercise modalities in mental health indicators remain scarce. Therefore, this study aimed to compare mental health indicators between older men practising aquatic physical exercise and older men practising multicomponent physical exercise.

title: Primary borderline retroperitoneal mucinous cystic neoplasm and situs inversus totalis: a case report
creator: Jeude M S Bravo, Igor V Cangussu, Priscila T Tanuri, Giovanna A Rosa, Vaine G S Ribeiro, João Lucas G Correa, Lúcio Fernando D Cachaca, Frederico Augustus M Resende, Eliel O De Araújo
description: Primary retroperitoneal mucinous cystic neoplasms (PRMCNs) are rare tumors classified into cystadenoma, PRMCN with borderline malignancy (PRMCN-BM), and cystadenocarcinoma. We report a 60-year-old woman with left flank abdominal pain whose MRI revealed situs inversus totalis alongside a complex cystic lesion in the left retroperitoneum measuring 4.8 × 5.2 × 4.5 cm.

title: Optimized protocol for quantification of extracellular nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide: evaluating clinical parameters and pre-analytical factors for translational research
creator: Al-Hussein Ahmed Saqr, Can Kamali, Philipp Brunnbauer, Nils Haep, Pia Koch, Karl-Herbert Hillebrandt, Eriselda Keshi, Simon Moosburner, Raphael Mohr, Nathanael Raschzok, Johann Pratschke, Felix Krenzien
description: Nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD+), a coenzyme for more than 500 enzymes, plays a central role in energy production, metabolism, cellular signaling, and DNA repair. Until recently, NAD+ was primarily considered to be an intracellular molecule (iNAD+), however, its extracellular species (eNAD+) has recently been discovered and has since been associated with a multitude of pathological conditions.

title: Combined Association of High-Sensitivity C-Reactive Protein and Vitamin D with Short-Term Functional Outcomes in Acute Ischemic Stroke
creator: Seongmin Choi, Yunjung Rho, Min-Su Kim, Myung Chul Yoo, Ga Yang Shim, Jin San Lee, Sung Joon Chung, Yunsoo Soh
description: Background/Objectives: Whether high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hsCRP) and vitamin D (Vit D) provide complementary prognostic information for acute ischemic stroke is unclear. We examined the separate and joint associations of serum hsCRP and Vit D levels with short-term functional outcomes after acute ischemic stroke.

title: Toward Intelligent Chemical Mechanical Polishing: Integrating Multiscale Modeling and Machine Learning
creator: Xin Wu, Quanzhou Yao
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Chemical mechanical polishing (CMP) remains the cornerstone planarization technology in advanced semiconductor manufacturing. As device architectures transition toward FinFETs, gate-all-around structures, heterogeneous integration, and wide-bandgap semiconductors, CMP must simultaneously deliver angstrom-level flatness, high selectivity, low damage, and improved sustainability. Against this background, research in CMP is moving beyond empirical trial-and-error toward a more integrated paradigm that combines consumables design, physics-based modeling, and data-driven intelligence. This review systematically summarizes recent progress in CMP from four interrelated perspectives.

title: Willingness to institutionalize a relative with dementia: a web-platform assessment with the Portuguese adapted version of the Desire-to-Institutionalize Scale
creator: Soraia Teles, Milaydis Sosa Napolskij, Oscar Ribeiro, Sara Alves, Alberto Freitas, Ana Ferreira, Constança Paúl
description: IntroductionOlder persons with dementia (PwD) are more likely to be institutionalized than their counterparts without dementia. The caregiver’s desire to institutionalize has been suggested as the most important predictor of actual institutionalization. This cross-sectional study aimed to culturally adapt the Desire to Institutionalize Scale (DIS) to a country with a high prevalence of dementia (Portugal) and examine its psychometric properties.

title: IgM- and IgA-Enriched Polyclonal Intravenous Immunoglobulin Therapy in Sepsis: A Single-Center Retrospective Cohort Study
creator: Hakan Yılmaz, Melek Tulunay, Ali Abbas Yılmaz
description: Background/Objectives: Evidence for adjunctive intravenous immunoglobulin therapy in sepsis remains conflicting. This study evaluated the association of IgM- and IgA-enriched polyclonal intravenous immunoglobulin (IgGAM) therapy with clinical outcomes, including post hoc analyses according to initial empiric antibiotic therapy (IEAT) appropriateness.

title: Application of hybrid fuzzy interval-based machine learning models on financial time series — A case study of Taiwan biotech index during the epidemic period
creator: Hsio-Yi Lin, Bin-Wei Hsu
description: In recent years, the use of machine learning to predict stock market indices has emerged as a vital concern in the FinTech domain. However, the inherent nature of point estimation in traditional supervised machine learning models leads to an almost negligible probability of achieving perfect predictions, significantly constraining the applicability of machine learning prediction models.

title: AI-Assisted Analysis of Sentiment Changes Among Repeat Users of Digital Peer Support: A Retrospective Longitudinal Study
creator: Farbod Sedaghati, Anya Stetsenko, Ilayda Ozsan McMillan, Zara Dana, Harpreet Nagra
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Background: Digital peer support (DPS) is a scalable tool to provide emotional support across diverse user populations. Previous studies were limited to single-session outcomes, while the impact of repeated DPS sessions is not well understood. Objectives: This study evaluated sentiment trajectories among repeat users of a 24/7, anonymous, real-time moderated DPS service and examined whether DPS engagement across repeated sessions was associated with changes in negative sentiments (depression, loneliness, despair, grief, and work-related stress).

title: Explaining graph convolutional network predictions for clinicians—An explainable AI approach to Alzheimer's disease classification
creator: Sule Tekkesinoglu, Sara Pudas
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). IntroductionGraph-based representations are becoming more common in the medical domain, where each node defines a patient, and the edges signify associations between patients, relating individuals with disease and symptoms in a node classification task. In this study, a Graph Convolutional Networks (GCN) model was utilized to capture differences in neurocognitive, genetic, and brain atrophy patterns that can predict cognitive status, ranging from Normal Cognition (NC) to Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI) and Alzheimer's Disease (AD), on the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) database.

title: Implementing a provisional overarching intervention for COVID-19 monitoring and control in the Brazil-Colombia-Peru frontier
creator: Matilde Contreras, Felipe Gomes Naveca, Jose Joaquin Carvajal-Cortes, Guilherme F. Faviero, Jorge Saavedra, Eduardo Ruback dos Santos, Valdinete Alves do Nascimento, Victor Costa de Souza, Fernanda Oliveira do Nascimento, Dejanane Silva e Silva, Sérgio Luiz Bessa Luz, Kelly Natalia Romero Vesga, Jua
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Introductionhe challenge was to provide comprehensive health resources to a remote and underserved population living in the Brazil-Colombia-Peru border, amid the most disruptive global crisis of the century.MethodsIn August 2021, Fundação Oswaldo Cruz Amazonia (FIOCRUZ Amazônia) and partner collaborators implemented an overarching provisional program for SARS-CoV-2 detection and lineages characterization, training of laboratory personnel and healthcare providers, donation of diagnostic supplies and personal protective equipment, and COVID-19 vaccination.

title: Cannabigerol Modulates Blood Pressure and Vascular Reactivity in a Rat Model of Hypertension and Platelet Responses in Human Blood In Vitro
creator: Anna Krzyżewska, Krzysztof Mińczuk, Tomasz Misztal, Monika Kloza, Hanna Kozłowska
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Cannabigerol (CBG) exerts vasorelaxant effects in human pulmonary arteries and lowers blood pressure (BP) in normotensive mice. However, data on the cardiovascular effects of CBG in hypertension and platelet function remain limited.

title: The role of meteorological factors on influenza incidence among children in Guangzhou China, 2019–2022
creator: Zhitao Chen, Yanhui Liu, Haiyan Yue, Jinbin Chen, Xiangzhi Hu, Lijuan Zhou, Boheng Liang, Guozhen Lin, Pengzhe Qin, Wenru Feng, Dedong Wang, Di Wu
description: ObjectiveAnalyzing the epidemiological characteristics of influenza cases among children aged 0–17 years in Guangzhou from 2019 to 2022. Assessing the relationships between multiple meteorological factors and influenza, improving the early warning systems for influenza, and providing a scientific basis for influenza prevention and control measures.MethodsThe influenza data were obtained from the Chinese Center for Disease Control and Prevention.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Large Language Models in Surgical Shared Decision-Making and Informed Consent: A Narrative Review
creator: Nikoleta Koliou, Lazaros Kourtidis, Panagis M. Lykoudis, Ioannis Karavolias, Stavriana Charalampous, Georgios D. Ayiomamitis, Pinelopi Kouki, Christos A. Iordanou
description: Background: Artificial intelligence (AI) and large language models (LLMs) may make surgical information easier to access and understand. However, these tools cannot replace the clinician’s role in shared decision-making or the requirements for valid informed consent. Methods: This narrative review follows the surgical patient pathway from diagnosis and explanation to option comparison, shared decision-making, and informed consent.

title: Risk of newly diagnosed interstitial lung disease after COVID-19 and impact of vaccination: a nationwide population-based cohort study
creator: Bo-Guen Kim, Hyun Lee, Cho Yun Jeong, Sang Woo Yeom, Dong Won Park, Tai Sun Park, Ji-Yong Moon, Tae-Hyung Kim, Jang Won Sohn, Ho Joo Yoon, Jong Seung Kim, Sang-Heon Kim
description: ObjectivesPrevious studies suggested that coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) could lead to pulmonary fibrosis, but the incidence of newly diagnosed interstitial lung disease (ILD) after COVID-19 is unclear. We aimed to determine whether COVID-19 increases the risk of newly diagnosed ILD and whether vaccination against COVID-19 can reduce this risk.

title: Clinical Characteristics and Outcomes of Patients Undergoing Pericardiocentesis for Pericardial Effusion: A Single-Center Experience with Exploratory Inflammatory Biomarker Analysis
creator: Zeynep Yapan Emren, Gamze Erkılınç
description: Objective: We aim to characterize patients undergoing pericardiocentesis for clinically significant pericardial effusion and explore differences in inflammation-based biomarkers according to malignancy status and one-year outcome. Methods: We retrospectively evaluated 113 consecutive patients who underwent pericardiocentesis between January 2021 and January 2026. Clinical, laboratory, pericardial fluid, cytopathological, recurrence, and mortality data were analyzed.

title: Stress is not so bad—cortisol level and psychological functioning after 8-week HIIT program during pregnancy: a randomized controlled trial
creator: Dominika Wilczyńska, Tamara Walczak-Kozłowska, Rita Santos-Rocha, Radosław Laskowski, Anna Szumilewicz
description: BackgroundAmid extensive pregnancy exercise research, the impact of High Intensity Interval Training (HIIT) on pregnant women’s mental health is underexplored. Despite exercise benefits, it can trigger stress responses like elevated cortisol. This study fills the gap by investigating correlations between hair cortisol levels, mental health, and HIIT effects in pregnant women.

title: Enhancing public health research: a viewpoint report on the transition to secure, cloud-based systems
creator: Plinio Pelegrini Morita, Jasleen Kaur, Pedro Augusto Da Silva E Souza Miranda
description: , disease trends, and effective interventions. Despite advancements in data availability, collection, and analysis (9–13), the use of PHI for research has been hindered by storage, cybersecurity, and data governance challenges (6–8, 14–18). PHI has traditionally been stored in local databases or filesystems which lack sufficient cybersecurity and data governance.

title: Epigenetic Clocks Can Predict Age in the Largemouth Bass‐Complex Despite Spatial and Sexual Variation
creator: Steven T Gardner, Daniel J Daugherty, Dijar Lutz‐Carrillo, Brenda Pracheil, Kristine N Moody
description: Sustainable fisheries rely on balancing harvests with ecological impacts. Despite the importance of species' demographic profiles, many assessments forgo age due to methodological complexities. Developing non‐lethal methods for age determination can improve stock assessments to ensure future sustainability. Epigenetic signals, specifically DNA methylation, are dynamic and considered to be associated with decreasing genomic stability with age.

title: The status quo of short videos as a health information source of Helicobacter pylori: a cross-sectional study
creator: Yongkang Lai, Foqiang Liao, Zixuan He, Weiguo Lai, Chunping Zhu, Yiqi Du, Zhaoshen Li
description: BackgroundHealth education about Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori) is one of the most effective methods to prevent H. pylori infection and standardize H. pylori eradication treatment. Short videos enable people to absorb and remember information more easily and are an important source of health education. This study aimed to assess the information quality of H.

title: Dementia and traumatic brain injuries: underestimated bidirectional disorder
creator: Ayman El-Menyar, Hassan Al-Thani, Mohamed Farouk Mansour
description: addition to the poor quality of studies, were of substantial concern. In general, the contemporary literature lacks enough data to explore the direction and interactions between dementia and trauma, including which one is a risk factor for the other and to which extent. Additionally, the link between cerebrovascular pathology, neuroinflammation, and the severity of trauma remains understudied (3, 4).

title: A Green Lindqvist-Type POM/TEMPO/H2O2 Ternary Catalytic System for the Selective Oxidation of Hantzsch 1,4-Dihydropyridines (1,4-DHPs) to Pyridines
creator: Qiang Zeng, Xiaoxiao Yan, Shaohong Hou, Yutong Zhang, Jiuzhong Huang, Gaorong Wu, Dan Miao, Feng Jiang, Weiming Chen
description: Pyridine derivatives are prepared via the dehydrogenative aromatization of 1,4-dihydropyridines (1,4-DHPs). Among these methods, stoichiometric catalysis with high waste and electrochemical oxidation with less productivity are limited in their use. Notably, methyl groups and nitrogen atoms may impose limitations on oxidation.

title: Development and Internal Validation of a Preoperative Risk Stratification Model for Difficult Laparoscopic Cholecystectomy in Acute Cholecystitis
creator: Sinan Aslan, Şebnem Çimen
description: Background: Difficult laparoscopic cholecystectomy (DLC) in patients with acute cholecystitis (AC) is associated with greater operative complexity and increased perioperative morbidity, yet reliable preoperative risk stratification remains limited. This study aimed to develop and internally validate a preoperative prediction model for DLC and to compare its predictive performance with that of an alternative C-reactive protein–albumin–lymphocyte (CALLY)-based model.

title: Effect of TMAO on the incidence and prognosis of cerebral infarction: a systematic review and meta-analysis
creator: Lin Wang, Yinan Nan, Wenhao Zhu, Shaoqing Wang
description: ObjectiveThis study aimed to evaluate the effect of trimethylamine oxide (TMAO) on the incidence and prognosis of cerebral infarction.MethodsWe searched PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane databases for all clinical studies on the association of TMAO with cerebral infarction incidence and prognosis from inception to April 2023.

title: Responses of Anti-Apoptotic Molecules to EAgNPs and EAgNPs Plus L-Buthionine-Sulfoximine in Human Tongue Cancer Cells
creator: Ximing Wu, Fuming Wang, Xiaoyu Huang, Mingchuan Yang, Yufeng He, Jinsong Zhang, Huali Wang
description: Silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) have emerged as a promising nanoplatform for oncological intervention, yet their clinical translation is severely hampered by systemic toxicities associated with high effective doses, while the underlying mechanisms governing their interactions with cancer cell pro-survival cascades remain poorly defined.

title: Prognostic value of CBV index in patients with acute ischemic stroke treated with endovascular thrombectomy in late therapeutic window
creator: Aicheng Sun, Yuezhou Cao, Zhenyu Jia, Linbo Zhao, Haibin Shi, Sheng Liu
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). PurposeTo evaluate the prognostic value of the cerebral blood volume (CBV) index for 90-day functional outcomes in patients with acute ischemic stroke (AIS) treated within a late therapeutic window.MethodsWe retrospectively reviewed patients who underwent pre-treatment computed tomography perfusion (CTP) and endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) for large-vessel occlusion (LVO) of the anterior circulation within the late therapeutic window between January 2021 and February 2023.

title: Blood Pressure-Lowering Effects of Finerenone: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials
creator: Gaetano Marino, Stefania Angela Di Fusco, Elvira Graziano, Sara Corradetti, Stefano Aquilani, Silvio Fedele, Federico Nardi, Domenico Gabrielli, Carmine Savoia, Furio Colivicchi
description: Background: Optimal blood pressure (BP) control remains elusive for millions of patients worldwide, often leading to resistant or secondary hypertension. Overactivation of the mineralocorticoid receptor (MR) drives this systemic pathology. While steroidal mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists (MRAs) are effective, their clinical utility is limited by poor cross-selectivity and risk of hyperkalemia.

title: Experimental Study on the Mechanical Performance of Large Plate Girders Under Eccentric Loading
creator: Yuxiang Zhang, Xiufeng Chen, Jinli Wei, Ju Chen
description: To investigate the mechanical performance of large plate girders used in boiler-supporting steel structures under eccentric loading, nine 1:5-scaled closed-section HK-type and open-section π-type specimens were designed and tested. The specimens had a span of 5960 mm, an overall length of 6220 mm, and a depth of 1760 mm.

title: Evaluation of Different Chemotypes of Lavandula angustifolia Essential Oils as Phytobiotics for the Control of Clinical Escherichia coli Strains Isolated from Commercial Poultry Production
creator: Michalina Adaszyńska-Skwirzyńska, Małgorzata Dzięcioł, Sławomir Zych
description: The study focused on evaluating the antibacterial activity of ten essential oils (EOs) representing different origins and chemotypes of common lavender (Lavandula angustifolia), as well as their two major constituents, linalool and linalyl acetate. The aim of the study was to evaluate their potential as natural phytobiotics against clinical Escherichia coli strains isolated from poultry, including multidrug-resistant avian pathogenic E.

title: The neonatal adverse event severity scale: current status, a stakeholders' assessment, and future perspectives
creator: Karel Allegaert, Thomas Salaets, Kelly Wade, Mary A. Short, Robert Ward, Kanwaljit Singh, Mark A. Turner, Jonathan M. Davis, Tamorah Lewis
description: To support informed decisions on drug registration and prescription, clinical trials need tools to assess the efficacy and safety signals related to a given therapeutic intervention. Standardized assessment facilitates reproducibility of results. Furthermore, it enables weighted comparison between different interventions, instrumental to facilitate shared decisions.

title: Design strategies for VR science and education games from an embodied cognition perspective: a literature-based meta-analysis
creator: Xiuyu Lin, Runbo Li, Zhirong Chen, Jiayi Xiong
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). IntroductionNatural science education, as an important means to improve the scientific literacy of citizens, combines science education games with virtual reality (VR) technology and is a major developmental direction in the field of gamified learning.MethodsTo investigate the impact of VR science education games on learning efficiency from the perspective of embodied cognition, this study uses the China National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI) and Web of Science (WOS) databases as the main source of samples.

title: Diagnostic Accuracy of a Novel Chemiluminescent Immunoassay for Strongyloides stercoralis in a Non-Endemic Clinical Setting
creator: Sara Roose, Lorenza Sanfilippo, Stefano Tais, Sara Negrelli, Eleonora Rizzi, Giulia Gambini, Francesca Tamarozzi, Francesca Perandin, Dora Buonfrate
description: Background/Objectives: Strongyloides stercoralis is a soil-transmitted helminth that can cause severe disease in immunocompromised individuals. In non-endemic clinical settings, recommended diagnostic strategies rely on serology alone or in combination with a sensitive fecal test, maximizing sensitivity to avoid missed infections. The S.

title: The impact of employees’ experience of high-performance work systems on innovative behavior in professional service firms
creator: Beenish Arshad, Hamid Hassan, Akbar Azam
description: This research examines the impact of employees’ experience of high-performance work systems (HPWS) on their innovative behavior. The study draws upon social exchange theory to propose that employees’ experience of HPWS influences their innovative behavior directly and through sequential mediation of social capital development and knowledge-sharing behavior.

title: The role of anticipated emotions in self-control: linking self-control and the anticipatory ability to engage emotions associated with upcoming events
creator: Johann D. Kruschwitz, Thomas Goschke, Elkhansa Ahmed Mohamed Ali, Anne-Carolin Kraehe, Franziska Maria Korb, Henrik Walter
description: Self-control is typically attributed to “cold” cognitive control mechanisms that top-down influence “hot” affective impulses or emotions. In this study we tested an alternative view, assuming that self-control also rests on the ability to anticipate emotions directed toward future consequences.

title: Interocular Differences in Visual Acuity and Refractive Status Between Unilateral Early and Late Age-Related Macular Degeneration: A Nationwide Population-Based Study
creator: Chang Gu Kang, Su Kang Kim, Hyungoo Kang, Sang-il Park
description: Background/Objectives: Age-related macular degeneration (AMD) may affect the two eyes asymmetrically, but visual impairment is commonly classified by visual acuity (VA) in the better-seeing eye. We compared interocular-presenting VA differences in unilateral early versus late AMD, assessed the association between late AMD and worse VA in the AMD-affected eye, and compared refractive status between the affected and fellow eyes.

title: A Small-Molecule TrkB Agonist Promotes Synaptic Resilience Against Aβ and Tau Oligomers and Mitigates Alterations in TrkB-Akt and Fyn Signaling
creator: Tao Yang, Kevin C. Tran, Albert Leng, Vanessa F. Langness, Stephen M. Massa, Frank M. Longo
description: Highlights What are the main findings? In vitro, PTX-BD4-3 protected against oAβ-induced synaptic protein loss and elevation of Fyn, NR2B, and tau phosphorylation. Preservation of synaptic proteins following oAβ exposure was TrkB-dependent. PTX-BD4-3 also protected against oTau-induced dendritic spine loss.

title: Biological functions and applications of LncRNAs in the regulation of the extracellular matrix in osteoarthritis
creator: Di Shi, Yufeng Mei, Wan Hao, Jun Li, Shuguang Liu, Xiao Lin
description: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a major cause of disability, characterized by chronic pain, irreversible destruction, and loss of function of the articular cartilage. The integrity and arrangement of the composition and structure of the extracellular matrix (ECM) are essential for maintaining the elasticity, integrity, and mechanical support function of the cartilage tissue.

title: Correction to: “Probabilistic quality assurance of biopsy DVH thresholds in HDR prostate brachytherapy under localization uncertainty”
creator: Unknown
description: ion of the original article, the referenced companion manuscript had not yet been published and was therefore cited using its pre‐publication title and status. The article has since been published with a revised title and final publication details. Current reference 31 Muscat M, Crook J, Jirasek A, Andrews J, Becker N.

title: microRNA and Regulatory Networks of Human Macrophage During Leishmania major In Vitro Infection
creator: Sara Habouria, Aymen Bali, Aurora Diotallevi, Ali Ben-Cheikh, Chiraz Atri, Mauro De Santi, Sara Maestrini, Luca Galluzzi, Dhafer Laouini, Fatma Zahra Guerfali
description: Leishmania (L.) major modulates host microRNA (miR) expression to promote intracellular survival, yet the roles of specific miRs during early infection of human macrophages remain poorly defined. We investigated the dynamic regulation of miR-21-5p and miR-146a-5p in THP-1-derived macrophages infected with L. major over an early post-infection time course (3–48 h), alongside miR-30a-3p and miR-101-3p.

title: Patient Satisfaction with Process-Related Aspects of Outpatient Physiotherapy Care: Preliminary Insights from Croatia
creator: Maroje Višić, Ivana Kos Tolić, Iva Lončarić Kelečić, Jasna Mesarić
description: Background: Patient satisfaction is an important indicator of healthcare quality, yet evidence on satisfaction with outpatient physiotherapy (OPT) in Croatian publicly funded primary care settings remains limited. Methods: This exploratory cross-sectional study examined patient evaluations of process-related aspects of OPT care and explored factors associated with variability in both composite and item-level ratings.

title: Intersectional Barriers to and Facilitators of Educational Inclusion for Persons With Disabilities in Low‐ and Middle‐Income Countries: A Systematic Literature Review
creator: Yusufu Simra, Shani Omari, Hussein Mwanjali
description: Backgroundin low‐ and middle‐income countries, the exclusion of persons with disabilities from education is influenced by a combination of structural, environmental, and psychosocial constraints. These challenges are further compounded by intersecting factors such as gender, socioeconomic status, and geographic location, which deepen existing inequalities. Gaining insight into these overlapping dynamics is essential for advancing inclusive education.

title: Nanoparticle-Enabled Immune-Dose Shaping in Breast Cancer Radiotherapy: Reconciling Tumor Immunogenicity with Systemic Immune Preservation
creator: Sorinel Lunca, Stefan Morarasu, Gabriel Mihail Dimofte
description: Radiotherapy can simultaneously promote tumor immunogenicity and damage the systemic immune compartments required to sustain antitumor responses. In breast cancer, radiation-induced lymphopenia is influenced by treatment geometry, irradiated volume, low-dose exposure, marrow and lymphoid irradiation, fractionation, and delivery characteristics, while nanoparticle radioenhancement can amplify tumor response through physical, redox, DNA-repair, and immune mechanisms.

title: Large-scale epidemiological analysis of common skin diseases to identify shared and unique comorbidities and demographic factors
creator: Qinmengge Li, Matthew T. Patrick, Sutharzan Sreeskandarajan, Jian Kang, J. Michelle Kahlenberg, Johann E. Gudjonsson, Zhi He, Lam C. Tsoi
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). IntroductionThe utilization of large-scale claims databases has greatly improved the management, accessibility, and integration of extensive medical data. However, its potential for systematically identifying comorbidities in the context of skin diseases remains unexplored.MethodsThis study aims to assess the capability of a comprehensive claims database in identifying comorbidities linked to 14 specific skin and skin-related conditions and examining temporal changes in their association patterns.

title: Basic Life Support Awareness, Knowledge, and Attitudes Among a Self-Selected Online Sample in the Aseer Region, Saudi Arabia: An Exploratory Cross-Sectional Survey
creator: Ibrahim Tawhari, Shahad Alshehri, Ahad Shafi Alaklabi, Raghad Jubran Alqahtani, Afaf Haif Qahtani, Baylasan Meraie E. Alqahtani, Reema Abdullah S. Alsharif, Danah Mansour Almutib, Ghala Ali Alshehri
description: Background/Objectives: Basic life support (BLS) and cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) are essential emergency interventions. This exploratory study described BLS awareness, reported training, self-assessed and objectively scored CPR knowledge, and attitudes in a self-selected online sample of adults in the Aseer Region, Saudi Arabia, and examined how these constructs related to one another; it was not designed to estimate regional prevalence.

title: Single-cell profiling of CD11c+ B cells in atherosclerosis
creator: Tanyaporn Pattarabanjird, Prasad Srikakulapu, Brett Ransegnola, Melissa A. Marshall, Yanal Ghosheh, Rishab Gulati, Chistopher Durant, Fabrizio Drago, Angela M. Taylor, Klaus Ley, Coleen A. McNamara
description: Circulating CD11c+ B cells, a novel subset of activated B cells, have been linked to autoimmunity and shown to expand with age. Atherosclerosis is an age-associated disease that involves innate and adaptive immune responses to modified self-antigens. Yet, the expression of CD11c on specific B-cell subtypes and its link to atherosclerosis are poorly understood.

title: Placental Iron Homeostasis: Navigating the Delicate Balance Between Transport and Ferroptosis
creator: Dariusz Szukiewicz
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). As an essential micronutrient, iron plays a vital role in oxygen transport, deoxyribonucleic acid synthesis, and energy production and is a redox-active cofactor for many biological processes. However, ferrous iron (Fe2+) is toxic to cells because it reacts with hydrogen peroxide in the Fenton reaction to generate the hydroxyl (free) radical, a key player in oxidative stress, leading to lipid peroxidation and iron-dependent cell death (ferroptosis). Therefore, iron homeostasis is precisely regulated.

title: Translational studies of exosomes in sports medicine – a mini-review
creator: Haoqiang Huang, Peng Chen, Xinting Feng, Yinhua Qian, Zhijian Peng, Ting Zhang, Qing Wang
description: This review in sports medicine focuses on the critical role of exosomes in managing chronic conditions and enhancing athletic performance. Exosomes, small vesicles produced by various cells, are essential for cellular communication and transporting molecules like proteins and nucleic acids. Originating from the endoplasmic reticulum, they play a vital role in modulating inflammation and tissue repair.

title: A Colorimetric Strategy for Arsenic(V) Determination in Rice via Boosting the Peroxidase-like Activity of NCuzyme
creator: Lei Xu, Mao-Ling Luo, Shan Qiu, Jing-Jing Dai, Huan Zhu, Feng-Qing Yang
description: Arsenic (As) is extremely poisonous, and prolonged exposure greatly raises the likelihood of developing cancer. It is crucial to develop selective and sensitive methods for detecting As. In this study, using melamine and Cu(II), a Cu-based complex (NCuzyme) with peroxidase (POD)-like activity was prepared using a green and simple approach for the first time.

title: COVID-19 infection characteristics, risk factors and its potential impacts on Takayasu arteritis: a web-based survey in a large cohort
creator: Xiufang Kong, Jinghua Wang, Guihua Fan, Huijing Huang, Ying Sun, Huiyong Chen, Lili Ma, Yanshan Li, Lindi Jiang
description: ObjectivesTo investigate the characteristics of COVID-19 and its impact on patients with Takayasu’s arteritis (TAK).MethodsA web-based survey was administered to a TAK cohort and their co-residents in China during January 2023. Infection symptoms, post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC), potential impacts of COVID-19 on patients’ disease condition, treatment and immune-related parameters were analyzed.

title: AI Dependency, Academic Self-Efficacy, and Depressive Symptoms Among Medical Students: A Structural Equation Modeling Study in Saudi Arabia
creator: Saeed Asiri
description: Background: The rapid integration of artificial intelligence (AI) tools into medical education has opened up new possibilities for academic support. However, it has also raised concerns about over-dependence on AI. Students’ use of AI may have implications for students’ academic self-concept and psychological well-being, but the interrelationships among these constructs are not yet sufficiently understood.

title: Rapid and Efficient Extraction of Chlorogenic Acid from Honeysuckle Using Microwave-Assisted Deep Eutectic Solvents: Process Optimization and Mechanistic Investigation via Integration of Experiments and Density Functional Theory Calculations
creator: Hongwei Wu, Ruixin Chen, Hu Feng, Ningfei Liu, Yongli Shi, Feng Wang, Tiancheng Mu
description: Chlorogenic acid (CA), the principal bioactive constituent of honeysuckle, is conventionally extracted by time-consuming methods using toxic organic solvents, which carry the risk of thermal degradation. This study provides a rapid and efficient microwave-assisted deep eutectic solvent (DES-MAE) method for CA extraction and elucidates its mechanism at the molecular level.

title: Applicability of electronic sphygmomanometer use in high-altitude areas according to the AAMI/ESH/ISO collaboration statement
creator: Xueting Liu, Runyu Ye, Xin Zhang, Wen Huang, Lirong Sun, Xingwei Huo, Xiaoping Chen
description: ObjectiveMercury sphygmomanometer (MS) has now been less and less used and no new devices have been manufactured (according to Minamata convention 2013). The application of the electronic sphygmomanometer (ES) in clinical practice has become increasingly common. However, reliable evidence for the use of the ES in high-altitude areas remains scarce.

title: Abolition by design: implementing the dismantling of the commercial tobacco and nicotine industry
creator: Raglan Maddox, Shane Kawenata Bradbrook
description: The commercial tobacco and nicotine industry continues to drive preventable disease and death globally. Despite progress in tobacco control, industry power, product diversification, market expansion, and policy interference have constrained the impact of incremental regulatory approaches. Downstream interventions, such as cessation supports and lung cancer screening, remain essential but respond to accumulated harms rather than preventing exposure at its source.

title: Prevalence and factors associated with medication adherence in children with central precocious puberty: a cross-sectional study
creator: Chunsong Yang, Xia Song, Jin Wu, Lingli Zhang
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Objectives: This study aimed to investigate the prevalence and influencing factors of medication adherence in children with central precocious puberty (CPP), and provide references for clinical practice. Methods: Children under 12 years of age with CPP and their caregivers at a women’s and children’s hospital were selected for a cross-sectional study from February to May 2023, and a questionnaire was used to collect basic characteristics of pediatric patients and their caregivers, information of medication, cognition of medication, and medication adherence.

title: Efficacy and safety of docetaxel plus S-1-based therapy in gastric cancer: a quantitative evidence synthesis of randomized controlled trials
creator: Hui-Fen Lv, Li-Feng Qin, Rui-Zhi Ran, Xue-Ping Jiang, Fang-Yu Zhao, Bo Li
description: Objective: To systematically evaluate the safety and efficacy of docetaxel plus S-1-based therapy in gastric cancer treatment. Methods: PubMed, Embase, The Cochrane Library, and Web of Science electronic databases were searched for randomized controlled trials on docetaxel plus S-1-based therapy in the treatment of gastric cancer from the establishment of the database to 1 September 2022.

title: Dynamic Co‐Evolution of C‐Reactive Protein and Albumin in Early Sepsis: A Group‐Based Dual‐Trajectory Analysis for Risk Stratification
creator: Tengfei Chen, Shuwen Zhang, Maoyu Ding, Yumei Yang, Qinxiang Yang, Wei Guo, Xiaolong Xu, Qingquan Liu
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The coupled evolution of inflammation and metabolic dysfunction during early sepsis is incompletely characterized. Although C‐reactive protein (CRP) and albumin (ALB) are established markers of these processes, their joint longitudinal patterns have rarely been examined. We used group‐based dual‐trajectory modelling (GBDTM) to identify distinct coevolutionary patterns of CRP and ALB and to evaluate their associations with mortality in patients with sepsis.

title: Gut Microbiota‐Dependent Tryptophan Metabolism Drives the Therapeutic Effects of Baitouweng Tang in Colitis via the AhR Pathway
creator: Chun Niu, Yongli Hua, Jianguo Kang, Fang Li, Baoxia Chen, Rongxia Guo, Yanming Wei
description: With dysregulation of the gut microbiota and its metabolic byproducts playing a pivotal role in inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) pathogenesis. Baitouweng Tang (BTWT), a traditional herbal formulation, has long been employed to treat gastrointestinal disorders and shows promising potential in the management of IBD. However, its precise pharmacological mechanisms remain elusive.

title: Constitutive expression of spliced X-box binding protein 1 inhibits dentin formation in mice
creator: Qian Xu, Jiahe Li, Hua Zhang, Suzhen Wang, Chunlin Qin, Yongbo Lu
description: Upon endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress, inositol-requiring enzyme 1 (IRE1) is activated, which subsequently converts an unspliced X-box binding protein 1 (XBP1U) mRNA to a spliced mRNA that encodes a potent XBP1S transcription factor. XBP1S is essential for relieving ER stress and secretory cell differentiation.

title: Distinguishing Strain Field Visualization Stability from Condition-Level Incremental Strain Accuracy in High-Temperature 2D Digital Image Correlation
creator: Yan Wang, Xiaoshan Ma, Xuan Zhang, Xiaofang Yang, Yu Pei, Huilong Zheng
description: High-temperature two-dimensional digital image correlation (2D-DIC) can produce spatially unstable strain fields and biased condition-averaged incremental strains, but these error signatures need not respond to the same processing. A smoother strain field is therefore not, by itself, evidence of improved scalar accuracy. We evaluated strain field visualization stability separately from extensometer-referenced, condition-level incremental strain accuracy.

title: Future Outlook Toward Heavy‐Metal‐Free Metal Chalcogenide Nanocrystals for Optoelectronic Applications
creator: Apurba Mahapatra, Ayon Das Mahapatra, Dipanjan Maity, Samrat Das Adhikari, Manoranjan Mandal, Alexander Eychmüller, Daniel Prochowicz, Fabian Paulus
description: Colloidal nanocrystals (NCs) represent a transformative class of materials for next‐generation optoelectronic devices, including photodetectors (PDs), photovoltaics (PVs), catalysis, and light‐emitting diodes (LEDs). Historically, research in this field has been dominated by toxic heavy‐metal‐based systems (Cd, Pb, Hg), but it is now undergoing a critical shift toward sustainability, driven by health concerns and RoHS regulations.

title: A Human–Machine Interaction–Experience–Learning Algorithm for Integrated Lateral–Longitudinal Decision-Making and Control in Intelligent Connected Vehicles
creator: Wenxuan Shen, Cunyue Yan, Zhaoqiang Wang, Zeng Huang, Wei Gao
description: Highlights What are the main findings? A human-preference reward shaping mechanism is proposed to constrain the policy search space in DRL-based autonomous driving, achieving 1.7 s earlier braking than the DDPG-RRT* baseline.A Kalman filter-based V2X communication anomaly compensation module is designed to ensure stable state estimation under packet loss, thereby enhancing the robustness of the system under non-ideal communication conditions.

title: Neural mechanisms involved in female mate choice in invertebrates
creator: Sagrario Cordero-Molina, Ingrid Fetter-Pruneda, Jorge Contreras-Garduño
description: Mate choice is a critical decision with direct implications for fitness. Although it has been recognized for over 150 years, our understanding of its underlying mechanisms is still limited. Most studies on mate choice focus on the evolutionary causes of behavior, with less attention given to the physiological and molecular mechanisms involved.

title: Functional Mitral Regurgitation Trajectories in CRT-Treated HFrEF During Medical Therapy Optimization: Association with Reverse Remodeling
creator: Oana Pătru, Silvia Luca, Dragoș Cozma, Bogdan Enache, Liviu Cirin, Mirela Virtosu, Maria-Laura Crăciun, Constantin-Tudor Luca, Simona Ruxanda Drăgan
description: Background: Functional mitral regurgitation (MR) is common in patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) and may persist despite cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT). Sacubitril/valsartan is associated with reverse remodeling in HFrEF, but MR dynamics in CRT-treated patients receiving sacubitril/valsartan remain insufficiently characterized.

title: Expression of placental CD146 is dysregulated by prenatal alcohol exposure and contributes in cortical vasculature development and positioning of vessel-associated oligodendrocytes
creator: Camille Sautreuil, Maryline Lecointre, Jessica Dalmasso, Alexis Lebon, Matthieu Leuillier, François Janin, Matthieu Lecuyer, Soumeya Bekri, Stéphane Marret, Annie Laquerrière, Carole Brasse-Lagnel, Sophie Gil, Bruno J. Gonzalez
description: Recent data showed that prenatal alcohol exposure (PAE) impairs the “placenta–brain” axis controlling fetal brain angiogenesis in human and preclinical models. Placental growth factor (PlGF) has been identified as a proangiogenic messenger between these two organs. CD146, a partner of the VEGFR-1/2 signalosome, is involved in placental angiogenesis and exists as a soluble circulating form.

title: The Myopic Normal Tension Glaucoma Treatment Study (MYNT-GTS): Protocol and Baseline Characteristics of a Randomized Controlled Trial
creator: Eun Ji Lee, Joon Mo Kim, Jiwoong Lee, Sangwoo Moon, Sang Woo Park, Mi Sun Sung, Ji-Ah Kim, Gyu-Nam Kim, Jong Chul Han, Ji Eun Song, Kyoung Min Lee, Tae-Woo Kim
description: Background/Objectives: To describe the study protocol and baseline characteristics of participants in the Myopic Normal-Tension Glaucoma Treatment Study (MYNT-GTS), which is a randomized controlled trial evaluating the effect of intraocular pressure (IOP)-lowering treatment on glaucoma progression in eyes with myopic normal-tension glaucoma (NTG). Methods: A prospective, multicenter, randomized controlled clinical trial and baseline cross-sectional analysis.

title: Is There a Relationship Between the Gut Microbiome and the Functional Capabilities of Skeletal Muscle? A Narrative Review
creator: Kristin S. Ondrak, Evan A. Seicshnaydre, Sharon J. Duffy, Corinna L. Rodriguez, Cassidy Scott, Sheri Gladish, Lauri O. Byerley
description: Diet is one of the primary determinants of gut microbiota composition and its metabolic output. That output is emerging as a critical determinant of systemic health and has been linked to most physiological systems in the body, yet its relationship to skeletal muscle physiology has only recently received attention.

title: Pre-Resection Endoscopic Features in T1 Colorectal Cancer Selected for Salvage Surgery After ESD/EID: An Exploratory Comparison of SM1 and SM2–3 Invasion
creator: Kasper Maryńczak, Julia Adamkiewicz, Jacek Kabziński, Aleksandra Osielczak, Przemysław Kasprzyk, Adam Dziki, Michał Spychalski, Ireneusz Majsterek, Łukasz Dziki
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Background/Objectives: Accurate assessment of submucosal invasion is important when selecting patients with early colorectal cancer for organ-preserving treatment. Endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD) and endoscopic intermuscular dissection (EID) enable en bloc resection and detailed histopathological assessment. This study explored whether routinely recorded pre-resection endoscopic characteristics differed between SM1 and SM2–3 lesions within a selected cohort of patients who underwent salvage surgery after non-curative endoscopic resection.

title: Biological response of nonhuman primates to controlled levels of acute blood loss
creator: Juhye Roh, Eun Mi Park, Haneulnari Lee, Jeong Ho Hwang, Hyung-Sun Kim, Jinyoung Park, Hee Jung Kang
description: IntroductionThe global shortage of human blood for medical use has prompted the development of alternative blood sources. Nonhuman primates (NHPs) are commonly used owing to their physiological similarities to humans. The objective of the current study was to establish a controlled-blood-loss model in NHPs to explore their clinical and biological responses.

title: Implementation of a Structured Perioperative Checklist-Based Standardization Process and Early Postoperative Outcomes After Bariatric Surgery: A Single-Center Retrospective Pre–Post Cohort Study
creator: Sertaç Ata Güler, Mehmet Fatih Özsaray, Turgay Şimşek, Nuh Zafer Cantürk
description: Background/Objectives: Structured perioperative checklists may standardize bariatric surgical care, but their association with early clinical outcomes remains uncertain. This study compared 30-day postoperative outcomes before and after implementation of a structured perioperative checklist and characterized complications by type and Clavien–Dindo severity. Methods: This single-center retrospective pre–post cohort study included patients undergoing primary bariatric surgery from June 2024 through December 2025.

title: PD-1/PD-L1 immune checkpoint therapy demonstrates favorable safety profile in patients with autoimmune and cholestatic liver disease
creator: Lorenz Kocheise, Ignazio Piseddu, Joscha Vonderlin, Eric T. Tjwa, Gustav Buescher, Lucy Meunier, Pia Goeggelmann, Francesca Fianchi, Jérôme Dumortier, Mar Riveiro Barciela, Tom J. G. Gevers, Benedetta Terziroli Beretta-Piccoli, Maria-Carlota Londoño, Sona Frankova, Thomas Roesner, Vincent Joerg, Con
description: IntroductionImmune checkpoint inhibitors (ICI) have revolutionized the treatment of many malignancies in recent years. However, immune−related adverse events (irAE) are a frequent concern in clinical practice. The safety profile of ICI for the treatment of malignancies in patients diagnosed with autoimmune and cholestatic liver disease (AILD) remains unclear.

title: Transcriptomic Profiling of Adherent Cells Isolated from Wedged Pulmonary Arterial Blood of Patients with Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension Reveals a Predominantly Myeloid Rather than Endothelial Phenotype
creator: Nadezhda Boyarskaya, Polina Kuchur, Pavel Docshin, Olga Skortsanu, Daria Smirnova, Natalia Goncharova, Elizaveta Korobchenko, Kirill Lapshin, Olga Moiseeva, Anna Malashicheva
description: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) is characterized by progressive vascular remodeling and immune dysregulation. Myeloid angiogenic cells (MACs) are blood-derived mononuclear cells that acquire endothelial-like features at sites of vascular injury, but their transcriptomic phenotype in the pulmonary vascular compartment is poorly characterized.

title: Red–Blue and White Supplementary Light Increase Carotenoid Accumulation and Improve Fruit Quality in Satsuma Mandarin: Associations with Chlorophyll Content and Carotenogenic Gene Expression
creator: Wei Hu, Wenli Yu, Dechun Liu, Zhonghua Xiong, Li Yang, Liuqing Kuang, Jie Song, Jingheng Xie, Yong Liu
description: Light regulates plant growth and secondary metabolism. To improve the nutritional quality and economic benefits of satsuma mandarin (Citrus unshiu Marc.) under greenhouse conditions with reduced natural light, we investigated the effects of supplementary lighting with different light qualities and intensities on fruit coloration, carotenoid accumulation, and fruit quality.

title: Exploring KRAS-mutant pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma: a model validation study
creator: Fan Yang, Yanjie He, Nan Ge, Jintao Guo, Fei Yang, Siyu Sun
description: IntroductionPancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) has the highest mortality rate among all solid tumors. Tumorigenesis is promoted by the oncogene KRAS, and KRAS mutations are prevalent in patients with PDAC. Therefore, a comprehensive understanding of the interactions between KRAS mutations and PDAC may expediate the development of therapeutic strategies for reversing the progression of malignant tumors.

title: Trends in Hospitalizations of Patients with Idiopathic Inflammatory Myopathies: Long-Term Observational Study, 2010–2024
creator: Maria Dutsch-Wicherek, Bartłomiej Wieleba, Katarzyna Lewtak, Krzysztof Kanecki, Jakub Stokwiszewski, Małgorzata Wisłowska
description: Background/Objectives: Idiopathic inflammatory myopathies (IIMs) are very rare, chronic, immune-mediated diseases that clinically manifest with myositis symptoms and extramuscular manifestations. The rarity of the disease makes it difficult to conduct double-blind studies, and large population-based studies are needed to improve our knowledge of them. This study aims to analyze the hospitalization rates and trends of IIMs between 2010 and 2024.

title: Peat-Free Composted Bark and Wood Fiber Blends for Container Ornamentals: Species-Dependent Growth and Quality Responses
creator: Akinson Tumbure, Munno Prasad, Eoghan Corbett, Zoia A. Awan, Dónall Flanagan, Michael T. Gaffney
description: Identification of environmentally sustainable alternative materials or material blends capable of effectively replacing peat in ornamental horticulture is a significant global challenge. The present study involved five separate experiments with three growing media treatments consisting of two composted bark and wood fiber mixes (at 80:20 and 60:40; bark:wood fiber) and pure peat as control.

title: Do parent media habits contribute to child global development?
creator: Caroline Fitzpatrick, Alexa Johnson, Angélique Laurent, Mathieu Bégin, Elizabeth Harvey
description: Background/objectiveParents of preschoolers’ report using screen media frequently. More frequent screen use by parents may undermine child development by displacing time for foundational parent-child interactions. The objective of the present study is to examine the extent to which parent screen use contributes to child global development 1 year later.

title: MRI-Based Morphologic Patterns of the Peroneus Quartus in a Korean Clinical Cohort: An Anatomical Study with an Illustrative Surgical Case
creator: Otgonsaikhan Nomkhondorj, Ye-Chan Choi, Jeong-Hyun Park, Hyung-Wook Kwon, Digud Kim, Yu-Jin Choi, Yunil Choe, Kwang-Rak Park, Jaeho Cho
description: Background/Objectives: The peroneus quartus (PQ) is an accessory musculotendinous structure of the lateral leg with variable origin and distal attachment. Although its anatomy has been described in cadaveric and imaging studies, the morphologic patterns encountered on routine ankle MRI remain clinically relevant.

title: Explore the effects of forest travel activities on university students’ stress affection
creator: Wei-Yin Chang, Xin Wang, De-Sheng Guo, Lam-Huu-Phuoc Nguyen, Ngoc-Huy Tran, Shuai-Jie Yang, Hui-Zhong Lin, Hsiu-Chen Wu, Chin-Fei Huang
description: This study aims to explore the effects of forest travel activities on university students’ stress affection. Forty volunteer university students participated in this study. All participants were asked to complete physiological (Heart Rate Variability) and psychological (Brief Profile of Mood State and State–Trait Anxiety Inventory) tests before and after the travel activities.

title: A reinforcement learning model with choice traces for a progressive ratio schedule
creator: Keiko Ihara, Yu Shikano, Sae Kato, Sho Yagishita, Kenji F. Tanaka, Norio Takata
description: The progressive ratio (PR) lever-press task serves as a benchmark for assessing goal-oriented motivation. However, a well-recognized limitation of the PR task is that only a single data point, known as the breakpoint, is obtained from an entire session as a barometer of motivation.

title: Association of Nutritional Status at Diagnosis with Disease Course in Pediatric Inflammatory Bowel Disease
creator: Annalisa Morelli, Michela Caprarelli, Roberta Giusy Ruiz, Bianca Mazzoli, Alessia Salatto, Daniela Knafelz, Fiammetta Bracci, Sabrina Cardile, Giulia Bolasco, Chiara Maria Trovato, Paola De Angelis, Erminia Francesca Romeo, Antonella Diamanti
description: Background: Growth impairment is a major component of pediatric inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), yet the prognostic role of baseline nutritional status remains debated. We assessed the impact of nutritional status at diagnosis on subsequent medical and surgical disease course. Methods: We retrospectively studied 183 children with IBD (84 Crohn’s disease, 99 ulcerative colitis) followed for at least 18 months.

title: Comparative transcriptomic insights into the domestication of Pleurotus abieticola for coniferous cultivation
creator: Lei Sun, Frederick Leo Sossah, Yu Li, Huiying Sun
description: Introduction: Pleurotus abieticola, a promising edible fungus in the Pleurotaceae family, especially its ability to utilize coniferous substrate, holds significant potential for commercial cultivation. However, few reports on the adaptation of P. abieticola to coniferous substrate from the perspective of omics. Methods: This study explores the biological characteristics, domestication process, and nutritional composition of P.

title: Efficient and generalizable cross-patient epileptic seizure detection through a spiking neural network
creator: Zongpeng Zhang, Mingqing Xiao, Taoyun Ji, Yuwu Jiang, Tong Lin, Xiaohua Zhou, Zhouchen Lin
description: IntroductionEpilepsy is a global chronic disease that brings pain and inconvenience to patients, and an electroencephalogram (EEG) is the main analytical tool. For clinical aid that can be applied to any patient, an automatic cross-patient epilepsy seizure detection algorithm is of great significance.

title: Conducting research with Indigenous Peoples in Canada: ethical and policy considerations
creator: Dominique Morisano, Margaret Robinson, Brian Rush, Renee Linklater
description: The international context of Indigenous mental health and wellbeing has been shaped by a number of key works recognizing Indigenous rights. Despite international recognitions, the mental health and wellness of Indigenous Peoples continues to be negatively affected by policies that ignore Indigenous rights, that frame colonization as historical rather than ongoing, or that minimize the impact of assimilation.

title: Turkish Adaptation of the Clean Food Consumerism Scale: A Validity and Reliability Study
creator: Simge Sipahi Uygur, Nihan Çakır Biçer, Ece Öneş, Sena Roberts, Selen Köksal, Perim Fatma Türker, Murat Baş
description: Background: Clean food consumerism reflects consumers’ preferences for foods perceived as natural, authentic, transparent, and health-promoting. This study aimed to culturally adapt the Clean Food Consumerism Scale (CFCS) into Turkish and evaluate its psychometric properties. Methods: The CFCS was translated, back-translated, reviewed by experts, pilot-tested, and psychometrically evaluated.

title: Correlation and underlying brain mechanisms between rapid eye movement sleep behavior disorder and executive functions in Parkinson’s disease: an fNIRS study
creator: Lu Ren, Xiaoxue Yin, Hai-Yang Wang, Xinqing Hao, Da Wang, Feng Jin, Tingting Zhang, Tao Li, Tingting Zhou, Zhanhua Liang
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). PurposeRapid eye movement sleep behavior disorder (RBD) affects 30%–40% of patients with Parkinson’s disease (PD) and has been linked to a higher risk of cognitive impairment, especially executive dysfunction. The aim of this study was to investigate the brain activation patterns in PD patients with RBD (PD-RBD+) compared to those without RBD (PD-RBD−) and healthy controls (HCs), and to analyze the correlation between changes in cerebral cortex activity and the severity of RBD.MethodsWe recruited 50 PD patients, including 30 PD-RBD+, 20 PD-RBD−,

title: The role of effective factors on suicidal tendency of women in Turkey
creator: Şerife Kılıçarslan, Sefa Çelik, Abdullah Y. Güngör, Ömer Alkan
description: Background/AimThis study aims to identify the variables that influence the suicidal tendency of women who are married, have had a relationship or are currently in a relationship in Turkey.MethodsThis study uses cross-sectional data from the 2014 Hacettepe University Institute of Population Studies National Research on Domestic Violence Against Women in Turkey.

title: Nursing Process Competency Among Nursing Interns and Its Associated Psychological, Cognitive, and Environmental/Social Factors: A Cross‐Sectional Study
creator: Xinxue Xi, Jing Le, Chenxi Zhou, Keke Zhang, Tieying Zeng, Ying Wang, Jing Mao
