title: Rural Versus Urban Distribution of Obstetrics and Gynecology Residency Training and Associated Rural Community Characteristics
creator: Ryan Spencer, Mukesh Adhikari, Lori Rodefeld, Laney McDougal, AnnaMarie Connolly, Emily M. Hawes
description: PurposeTo assess the distribution of OB/GYN residency program training sites and compare community characteristics in rural counties with and without training sites.MethodsUsing data from the Accreditation Council for Graduate Medical Education (ACGME), the locations of all accredited obstetrician/gynecologist (OB/GYN) residency training sites for the 2023–2024 academic year (AY 23–24) were geocoded.

title: Systematic benchmarking of multi-ancestry fine-mapping under variant heterogeneity and LD mismatch
creator: Guangxin Chen, Peristera Paschou, Boran Gao
description: Increasingly diverse, multi-ancestry genome-wide association studies (GWASs) provide unprecedented opportunities to better understand the genetic architecture of complex traits. In particular, differences in linkage disequilibrium (LD) patterns across populations can be leveraged to improve the resolution and reliability of statistical fine-mapping.

title: Integration of an echocardiographic motion-management system into photon-based stereotactic arrhythmia radioablation planning
creator: Hans Oppitz, Amelie L Matusche, Laura Mantovani, Mathieu Kruska, Kerstin Siebenlist, Nour Alfakhouri, Adriano Garonna, Elisabetta Bonzano, Ester Orlandi, Viviana Vitolo, Adele Valentini, Nicoletta Basla, Frank A Giordano, Oliver Blanck, Roberto Rordorf, Jens Fleckenstein, Judit Boda-Heggemann, Lena
description: Background and purposeCardiorespiratory ultrasound motion monitoring may enhance the precision of dose delivery for stereotactic arrhythmia radioablation (STAR) of ventricular tachycardia. This treatment planning study aimed to evaluate the feasibility of photon-based STAR planning in the presence of an ultrasound probe.

title: The Influence of Microbiota on Wild Birds’ Parental Coprophagy Behavior: Current Advances and Future Research Directions
creator: Saba Gul, Yurou Shi, Jie Hu, Sen Song
description: This comprehensive review provides an in-depth exploration of the intriguing phenomenon of parental coprophagy in wild birds and its profound implications on the influence of adult avian parents’ health. This review investigates the composition and dynamics of avian feces’ microbiota, casting light on the various dietary, environmental, and genetic factors that influence its diversity.

title: Low‐Complexity Phase–Transition‐Based VO2 Transmissive Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface for Indoor Millimeter‐Wave Communications
creator: Junghyeon Kim, Sumin Bark, Minjae Lee, Sungjoon Lim
description: This paper presents a low‐complexity and low‐cost transmissive reconfigurable intelligent surface (TRIS) based on the phase‐change material vanadium dioxide (VO2) for indoor millimeter‐wave (mm‐wave) communications. Although mm‐wave systems enable ultra‐high data rates and low latency, their performance is limited by severe path loss and non‐line‐of‐sight propagation. RISs offer a promising solution by dynamically controlling electromagnetic wave propagation.

title: Application of Solution-Processed High-Entropy Metal Oxide Dielectric Layers with High Dielectric Constant and Wide Bandgap in Thin-Film Transistors
creator: Jun Liu, Xin Xiong, Han Li, Xiangchen Huang, Yajun Wang, Yifa Sheng, Zhihao Liang, Rihui Yao, Honglong Ning, Xiaoqin Wei, Ai-Qun Liu, Chengyuan Dong
description: High-k metal oxides are gradually replacing the traditional SiO2 dielectric layer in the new generation of electronic devices. In this paper, we report the production of five-element high entropy metal oxides (HEMOs) dielectric films by solution method and analyzed the role of each metal oxide in the system by characterizing the film properties.

title: Multi‐Objective Inverse Design of a Dual‐Narrowband Thermal Emitter for Optical Gas Sensing
creator: Xiaowen Li, Zilin Zhang, Jiazheng Tang, Sheng Liu, Jie Sheng, Qionghui Chang, Xuyang Zhang, Yuchuan Shao, Zhengji Wen, Feng Liu
description: Spectrally selective narrowband thermal emitters with high‐temperature stability are critical infrared sources for advanced gas sensing. However, conventional Tamm‐plasmon narrowband thermal emitters are commonly implemented as distributed Bragg reflectors on thin metal layers, which can restrict spectral tunability and complementary metal–oxide–semiconductor (CMOS) compatibility. Here, we propose a cost‐effective, CMOS‐compatible, lithography‐free, wafer‐scale aperiodic dual‐narrowband thermal emitter.

title: 750 V Breakdown in GaN Buffer on 200 mm SOI Substrates Using Reverse-Stepped Superlattice Layers
creator: Shuzhen You, Yilong Lei, Liang Wang, Xing Chen, Ting Zhou, Yi Wang, Junbo Wang, Tong Liu, Xiangdong Li, Shenglei Zhao, Jincheng Zhang, Yue Hao, Nam-Trung Nguyen
description: In this work, we demonstrated the epitaxial growth of a gallium nitride (GaN) buffer structure on 200 mm SOI (silicon-on-insulator) substrates. This epitaxial layer is grown using a reversed stepped superlattice buffer (RSSL), which is composed of two superlattice (SL) layers with different Al component ratios stacked in reverse order.

title: Biodiverse Management of Perennial Flower Margins in Farmland: Meandering Mowing by ‘Three-Strip Management’ to Boost Pollinators and Beneficial Insects
creator: Laurian Parmentier, Hannah Vanderstappen, Geert Haesaert
description: Simple SummaryIntensive farming has caused a sharp decline in beneficial insects like pollinators (such as bees and butterflies) and natural predators of crop pests. One way to address this is by sowing flower margins on farmland, which can boost biodiversity and the numbers of beneficial insects for pollination and pest control.

title: Decoupled Spectral Tuning and Polarization Locking in Twisted α‐MoO3 Polaritonic Crystals
creator: Zhichen Zhao, Jiayi Yuan, Yanzhen Yin, Gang Zhong, Junbo Xu, Qingdong Ou, Tao Jiang
description: Polaritonic crystals (PoCs), formed by integrating periodic lattices with two‐dimensional polaritonic materials, provide a powerful platform for nanoscale light manipulation and far‐field spectral engineering. However, far‐field spectral engineering in existing PoCs is primarily achieved through geometric redesign, requiring structural reconfiguration to access different spectral responses.

title: Adapting to Uncertainty: Foraging Strategies in Dinoponera quadriceps (Formicidae: Ponerinae)
creator: Igor Eloi, Waldemar Alves Silva-Neto, Wallisen Tadashi Hattori, Arrilton Araújo, Kazuki Tsuji
description: Simple SummaryWe conducted an investigation into the foraging behavior of Dinoponera quadriceps, which is an ant species that forages solitarily. The ants were subjected to a range of foraging scenarios that included varying distances to food sources, differing prey sizes, and varying capture success rates.

title: Efficacy and safety of Siddha regimen for management of mild to moderate iron deficiency anaemia amongst reproductive age-group women as compared to iron folic acid supplements: A protocol for an open labelled, multicentric randomized equivalence trial
creator: P Shanmugapriya, T Subathra, R Gayatri, N Chandan, Manish J Barvaliya, M Ramamurthy, I Sangeetha, Kalesh M Karun, G Senthilvel, Subarna Roy
description: BackgroundIron deficiency anaemia is the most prevalent dietary deficiency anaemia, affecting 30% of the global population. According to WHO (2019), anaemia affects 500 million women (15–49 years) globally. In India, 57.2% of women in this age group are anaemic despite the “Anaemia Mukt Bharat Programme”.

title: Abnormalities of IL-12 Family Cytokine Pathways in Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease Progression
creator: Corina-Daniela Ene, Ilinca Nicolae, Cristina Căpușă, Lorena Losi
description: Background and Objectives: Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease (ADPKD) is the most frequent genetic renal disease with a complex physiopathology. More and more studies sustain that inflammation plays a crucial role in ADPKD pathogenesis and progression. We evaluated IL-12 involvement in ADPKD pathophysiology by assessing the serum levels of its monomers and heterodimers.

title: Ultrafast Optical Hydrogen Modulator in a Palladium Hydride Nanoparticulate Thin Film
creator: Floriana Morabito, Paula H. Aguado, Luca Pedicone, Alessandro Baserga, Andrés R. Botello Méndez, Stefano Dal Conte, Christoph Gadermaier, Giulio Cerullo, Zeila Zanolli, Marcel Di Vece
description: Electro‐ and thermochromic materials change their optical properties through the physical movement of atomic species within thin films. This movement is induced by electric fields or high temperatures and occurs on the second to minute timescale. Ultrashort laser pulses can manipulate atomic positions on the femto‐ to picosecond timescale.

title: Life Participation in Parents of Children With CKD
creator: Anastasia Hughes, Andrea Matus Gonzalez, Anita van Zwieten, Chandana Guha, Simon Carter, Germaine Wong, Dale Coghlan, Amanda Dominello, Jonathan C Craig, Martin Howell, Siah Kim, Karine Manera, Colm O’Reilly, Javier Recabarren Silva, Angela Rejuso, Benedicte Sautenet, Nicole Scholes-Robertson, Amand
description: BackgroundThe caregiver burden among parents of children with chronic kidney disease (CKD) is high and can impair their life participation, which may in turn have negative consequences on their children’s care and outcomes. We aim to describe effects on life participation in parents of children with CKD, from the perspectives of their children, health professionals, and the parents themselves.

title: Sustainable Carotenoid Extraction from Macroalgae: Optimizing Microwave-Assisted Extraction Using Response Surface Methodology
creator: Andreia Lopes, Luísa Correia-Sá, Mónica Vieira, Cristina Delerue-Matos, Cristina Soares, Clara Grosso, Pabulo H Rampelotto
description: This study aimed at optimizing carotenoid extraction using the macroalga Himanthalia elongata (L.) S.F.Gray as a model. Firstly, traditional extraction procedures were employed, using various solvents and temperatures to enhance the extraction conditions. Once the most effective extraction conditions were identified, the study transitioned to a more efficient and environmentally friendly approach, microwave-assisted extraction (MAE).

title: Out of the shadows: Phosphatase PP2A promotes shade avoidance by dephosphorylating phytochrome‐interacting factor 7
creator: Brian C. Mooney
description: leaf blade area. These responses enable plants to grow beyond their neighbour's shadow and regain access to light (Casal, 2013). Leaves primarily absorb red (R) light while reflecting far‐red (FR) wavelengths. Plants detect vegetative shade by monitoring the ratio of R:FR light using the photoreceptor phytochrome B (phyB) (Reed et al., 1993).

title: Recent Breakthroughs in PET-CT Multimodality Imaging: Innovations and Clinical Impact
creator: Dildar Hussain, Naseem Abbas, Jawad Khan, Riemer HJA Slart, Mario Petretta
description: This review presents a detailed examination of the most recent advancements in positron emission tomography–computed tomography (PET-CT) multimodal imaging over the past five years. The fusion of PET and CT technologies has revolutionized medical imaging, offering unprecedented insights into both anatomical structure and functional processes.

title: Long-term metabolic regulation in the era of GLP-1 receptor agonists: An integrative review of Ayurvedic and biomedical perspectives
creator: Trupti Naikare, Manisha Waghulkar
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Obesity and type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) are chronic, relapsing, and multifactorial disorders arising from long-term dysregulation of metabolic, neuroendocrine, behavioral, and environmental systems. Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonists represent a major advance in contemporary metabolic pharmacotherapy.

title: Effect of an Exercise Intervention Program on BMI and Distance Covered in the 6 Min Walking Test (6MWT) in Obese Children
creator: Ourania Papadopoulou, Evangelia Desli, Elisavet-Anna Chrysochoou, Christos Kogias, Vasileios Liakos, Athina Sopiadou, Petrina Vantsi, Ilias Kallistratos, Paris Iakovidis, Kiriaki Tsiroukidou, Elpis Hatziagorou
description: Background/Objectives: Childhood obesity appears to be an alarmingly growing global threat. Current evidence has shown that obesity can be successfully managed with interventions targeting movement skills, motor coordination and physical activity. However, data concerning physiotherapy practice are limited. We aimed to assess the impact of therapeutic exercise on the 6-minute walk test (6-MWT) in obese children and adolescents.

title: Management of Grade II osteoarthritis (Azhal kilvayu) utilizing Siddha internal and external treatment modalities (Varmam and Thokkanam): A case report
creator: Nikil Niva John Raja, Susila Rathinam, Hema Nandhini Devi Veluchamy, Sridevi Lakshmikanthan
description: A 59-year-old female patient visited the clinic with complaints of pain in both knee joints, along with mild swelling that had persisted for three months. Radiographic examination revealed Grade II knee osteoarthritis (OA). Her treatment plan included Siddha therapeutic purgation (Agathiyar kulambu), Siddha internal medications (Parangipattai maathirai, Sangu Parpam maathirai), and Siddha external therapies (Varmam and Thokkanam).

title: Exploring the Links Between Coping Strategies, Emotional Intelligence, and Age in Adolescents with Neuromotor Disabilities
creator: Ioana Elena Cioca, Maria Veronica Morcov, Corina Sporea, Oana Alina Apostol, Angelo Pellegrini, Elena-Nicoleta Bordea
description: Background/Objectives: The aim of this study is to explore the relationship between emotional intelligence and coping strategies used by adolescents with disabilities, on the one hand to understand how emotional skills influence stress management and everyday challenges and, on the other hand, considering that it could help specialists to develop interventions and educational programs that support the improvement of emotional

title: Viability of reducing plastic waste disposal by utilization in hot mix asphalt: a multicriteria analysis with cost considerations
creator: Adnan Qadir, Uneb Gazder
description: Plastic waste is a non-biodegradable material which is extensively used in many applications, creating a critical environmental challenge of its disposal. Therefore, its utilization in large quantities as a recycled product in road infrastructure will mitigate ill effects occurring because of its dumping.

title: Resettlement, Employment, and Mental Health Among Syrian Refugee Men in Canada: An Intersectional Study Using Photovoice
creator: Nancy Clark, Gökce Yurdakul, Carla Hilario, Heba Elgharbawy, Nedal Izzden, Elias Moses, Muna Zaidalkilani, Jimmy T Efird
description: Context: The impact of forced migration on the mental health of refugee men is far-reaching and compounded by gendered masculinity, which shapes men’s access to employment and other resources. A gap in knowledge exists on the broader determinants of refugee men’s mental health.

title: Awareness and Knowledge of Developmental Coordination Disorder Among Healthcare Professionals in the Eastern Province of Saudi Arabia: A Cross-Sectional Study
creator: Abdulaziz A Al-Ahmari, Abdullah A Alshabaan, Ali A Almeer, Mohammed N AlKhater, Mohammed A Al-Ibrahim, Hassan H Altuwal, Alaeddin A Al-Dajani, Saleh A Alqahtani, Mohammed A Al-Omari, Abdullah K Almutairi, Faisal O AlQurashi, Cesar Fernández-de-las-Peñas
description: Developmental coordination disorder (DCD) is a lifelong neurological disorder impairing the coordination and planning of motor and sensory tasks. Its functional manifestation includes difficulties in various aspects of daily living, making early diagnosis and management essential. This cross-sectional, questionnaire-based study targeted healthcare providers in Saudi Arabia’s Eastern Province who work with children under the age of 18.

title: Binocular ultra-high-speed photography for measuring tennis ball speed and spin at impact
creator: Bo Shi, Bin Lv, Yi Wang
description: SummaryBall speed and spin at impact characterize tennis stroke quality, yet measuring both on an unmodified ball has required costly trackers or instrumented balls. We developed a synchronized binocular ultra-high-speed photography system recording at 2000 frames per second that reconstructs three-dimensional ball-center trajectories stereoscopically and recovers rotation from the natural seam texture by closed-form quaternion attitude estimation.

title: Integrative Transcriptomic and Target Metabolite Analysis as a New Tool for Designing Metabolic Engineering in Yeast
creator: Alejandro Lopez-Barbera, Nerea Abasolo, Helena Torrell, Nuria Canela, Salvador Fernández-Arroyo
description: Precision fermentation processes, especially when using edited microorganisms, demand accuracy in the bioengineering process to maximize the desired outcome and to avoid adverse effects. The selection of target sites to edit using CRISPR/Cas9 can be complex, resulting in non-controlled consequences. Therefore, the use of multi-omics strategies can help in the design, selection and efficiency of genetic editing.

title: Comprehensive clinical dosimetry in contact skin interventional radiotherapy (modern brachytherapy): Practical tips and tricks
creator: Bruno Fionda, Enrico Rosa, Elisa Placidi, Valentina Lancellotta, Pierpaolo Dragonetti, Maria Concetta La Milia, Martina De Angeli, Francesco Pastore, Mariangela Massaccesi, Piotr Wojcieszek, Frank-André Siebert, Maria Antonietta Gambacorta, Marco De Spirito, Luca Tagliaferri
description: PurposeContact interventional radiotherapy (cIRT) is an effective option for non-melanoma skin cancers, particularly in anatomically complex sites, where organ preservation, functional results, and cosmetic outcomes are relevant. This paper summarized practical dosimetric considerations in cIRT, focusing on the therapeutic window, surface curvature, boluses and air gaps, dose calculation algorithms, and 3D-printed devices.

title: Early optical coherence tomography biomarkers of radiation maculopathy following ruthenium-106 brachytherapy for uveal melanoma in long-term follow-up
creator: Weronika Mularska, Maciej Rybak, Łukasz Tomczyk, Iwona Rospond-Kubiak
description: PurposeNon-invasive tests to detect early symptoms of radiation maculopathy (RM) are of primary concern of recent research. This will allow identification of a group of patients who are particularly at risk of vision loss due to developing complications as well as treatment evaluation.

title: Hemoglobin in Submicron Particles (HbMPs) Is Stabilized Against Oxidation
creator: Pichayut Rerkshanandana, Xiaotong Zhao, Yu Xiong, Yao Chen, Axel Steffen, Saranya Chaiwaree, Chiraphat Kloypan, Axel Pruss, Radostina Georgieva, Hans Bäumler, Claus Jacob, Brandon Reeder
description: Superoxide dismutase (SOD) and Catalase (CAT) play a crucial role as the first line of defense antioxidant enzymes in a living cell. These enzymes neutralize the superoxide anion from the autooxidation of oxyhemoglobin (Oxy-Hb) and convert hydrogen peroxides into water and molecular oxygen.

title: Red Cell Distribution Width as a Marker of Disease Severity and In-hospital Mortality in Patients with ST-segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction
creator: Raj Raval, Sunita Gupta, Nitin Gupta, Mohammad Abu Bashar
description: BackgroundThe red cell distribution width (RDW) has been investigated as a predictive factor for complications and mortality in several critical illnesses, including cardiovascular diseases.ObjectiveThe current study aimed to assess the relationship of RDW with severity and in-hospital mortality in patients with ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI).

title: Modern brachytherapy modalities vs. external beam radiotherapy in post-operative non-melanoma skin cancer: A systematic review
creator: Wiedya K. Angeline, Hendriyo, Rudiyo, Juli Jamnasi, Sudibio, Julius Oentario, Vito Filbert Jayalie
description: PurposeFacial non-melanoma skin cancers (NMSCs) are primarily managed surgically, but adjuvant or definitive radiotherapy is indicated for high-risk or anatomically complex lesions. While electron-based external beam radiotherapy (EBRT) remains standard, high-dose-rate (HDR) brachytherapy modalities now utilize surface moulds, 3D-printed applicators, interstitial implants, and flap techniques.

title: The Reality of Evaluating Urine Spot Sodium and Urine Spot Sodium Creatinine Ratio in Furosemide Stress Test as a New Biomarker in Diagnosing Progressive AKI in Critically Ill
creator: Ranajit Chatterjee, Lalit Gupta
description: How to cite this article: Chatterjee R, Gupta L. The Reality of Evaluating Urine Spot Sodium and Urine Spot Sodium Creatinine Ratio in Furosemide Stress Test as a New Biomarker in Diagnosing Progressive AKI in Critically Ill. Indian J Crit Care Med 2024;28(12):1089–1090.

title: Radiation-Induced Xerostomia in Patients With Head and Neck Cancer Treated With Comprehensive Salivary Gland-Sparing Helical Tomotherapy Technique Based on a Back Propagation Artificial Neural Network
creator: Feng Teng, Qi Teng Liu, Ling Ling Meng, Zhong Jian Ju, Xiang Kun Dai, Xin Xin Zhang, Lin Ma
description: BackgroundThe aim was to create a back propagation artificial neural network (BPANN) model for gauging the risk of developing xerostomia (dry mouth) due to targeted radiotherapy in patients with head and neck cancer (HNC), who underwent comprehensive salivary gland-sparing helical tomotherapy (HT).

title: Ultrasound in Shock: Is It the Elusive Magic Bullet?
creator: Balaji Kannamani, Shrikanth Srinivasan
description: How to cite this article: Kannamani B, Srinivasan S. Ultrasound in Shock: Is It the Elusive Magic Bullet? Indian J Crit Care Med 2024;28(12):1091–1092.Keywords: Bedside ECHO, Cardiogenic shock, Emergency department, Rapid ultrasound, Rapid ultrasound in shock and hypotension exam, Shock, Ultrasonography, Undifferentiated type of shock We read with interest the systematic review by Dr Gupta et al.

title: GLP-1 receptor agonists in elective spine surgery: a systematic review of fusion outcomes, perioperative safety, and procedure-specific risk
creator: Vinicius Ricieri Ferraz, Bashar Dawoud, Philippe A. Mercier, Tobias A. Mattei
description: BackgroundGlucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) are increasingly used in patients with obesity and type 2 diabetes mellitus undergoing elective spine surgery. Although these agents may improve metabolic risk profiles, their associations with spinal fusion, perioperative complications, and procedure-specific outcomes remain incompletely defined.

title: Critical Care Nurses’ Knowledge on Prevention of Ventilator-associated Pneumonia: A Cross-sectional Study
creator: Sae'd M El-Kass, Heshmah A Alruwili, Musherh A Alrowily, Osama M Ellayan, Lama M El-Kass, Eman E Hijo, Asmaa A El-Bhtety, Reneh M Abusnan, Zahraa A Aljundy, Dina A Sehweil, Marah A El-Ghorra, Eman A Elhaweet
description: BackgroundThis study aims to assess the knowledge of Palestinian critical care nurses regarding the prevention of ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP), an acquired infection that affects critically ill patients on ventilators in hospitals. Nurses caring for these patients may not always be aware of the most effective methods to prevent VAP.

title: The microbiome in mind: Reflections on antibiotic prescription in primary care
creator: Nicolas D B. Roos
description: In this opinion piece, the author critically reflects on his own antimicrobial stewardship practices in primary care and the complex factors influencing antibiotic prescription, specifically in children.ContributionIn light of emerging evidence of the role of the microbiome in both health and disease, this piece raises a key question: Are we doing more harm than good?

title: Investigation of the Number of Falls and Fall Risk Factors in Geriatric Individuals Living in a Nursing Home
creator: Yasemin Ateş Sarı, Sevilay Seda Baş, Büşra Kalkan Balak, Bahar Anaforoğlu, Nezehat Özgül Ünlüer
description: ObjectiveFalls are a major cause of morbidity and mortality among older adults worldwide, highlighting the need to identify fall risk factors, particularly among nursing home residents. This study aimed to evaluate fall risk factors according to fall history in nursing home–dwelling geriatric individuals and to examine the association between these factors and the number of falls.

title: Vidian Nerve Schwannoma Extending Into the Foramen Rotundum in a Female Patient: A Case Report
creator: Je Ho Bang, Se Hyeon Jin, Su Jin Kim, Kun Hee Lee
description: Schwannomas are benign tumors that can develop in any part of a nerve containing Schwann cells. Skull base schwannomas are rare, representing approximately 4% of extracranial schwannomas. Among these, vidian nerve schwannomas are particularly uncommon, with only a few documented cases.

title: Development of bioinformatics competency framework to address labor market demands in Thailand
creator: Pathacha Suksakit, Dumnoensun Pruksakorn, Kamonnut Singkhamanan, Surasak Sangkhathat, Yotsawat Pomyen, Tanaporn Uengwetwanit, Saowalak Kalapanulak, Treenut Saithong, Weerayuth Kittichotirat, Teeraphan Laomettachit, Kanthida Kusonmano, Raphatphorn Navakanitworakul, Arinthip Thamchaipenet, Kanphavarit
description: Bioinformatics plays a pivotal role in advancing healthcare, agriculture, and biotechnology. However, in Thailand, expectations regarding workforce demand and the core competencies of bioinformatics graduates remain insufficiently defined. Survey findings reveal that the demand for bioinformatics graduates is predominantly concentrated in the public sector, with comparatively limited demand from the private sector.

title: The optimal number of lymph nodes examined for rectal cancer patients undergoing neoadjuvant long-course chemoradiotherapy
creator: Kexing Xi, Lin Feng, Tianlei Xu, Lin Zhang, Yuelu Zhu, Hui Fang, Haizeng Zhang
description: BackgroundNumerous studies have documented a reduction in the number of lymph nodes (LNs) examined and the number of metastatic LNs in rectal cancer patients as a consequence of neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy (NCRT). It is plausible that the current guidelines advocating a specific number of LNs to be examined in rectal cancer surgery may be inappropriate for patients undergoing neoadjuvant therapy.

title: Impact of Antimicrobial Therapy on Mortality and Readmission in Multidrug-Resistant Pseudomonas Infections: A Retrospective Study at Dammam Medical Complex
creator: Ali Alsaeed, Abdulaziz Almomen, Ali Jawad, Ahmed AlNasser, Hassan Alkhmis, Noura AlSaghiri
description: Multidrug-resistant (MDR) Pseudomonas aeruginosa presents a significant treatment challenge, necessitating effective antimicrobial options. This retrospective, single-center cohort study was conducted at Dammam Medical Complex and aimed to evaluate the comparative effectiveness and safety of ceftazidime-avibactam (CAZ-AVI), ceftolozane-tazobactam (C-T), and meropenem and colistin in treating MDR P. aeruginosa infections.

title: Sustainable enhancement of acidic soil fertility through integrated soil amendments: A metagenomic evaluation of fungal functional improvement
creator: Ireng Darwati, Muchamad Yusron, Tiwit Widowati, Edi Yatno, April Hari Wardhana, Gina Aliyah Sopha, Octivia Trisilawati, Devi Rusmin, Raden Vitri Garvita, Rudi Suryadi, Indarti Puji Lestari, Yati Haryati, Agustina E Br Marpaung, Muhammad Hikmat, Suryani, Tika Anggraeni
description: Acid soil is characterized by low pH, which restricts nutrient availability and disrupts overall soil biological functioning. Soil ameliorants, such as Hermetia illucens (black soldier fly; BSF) frass, lime, and biochar, are widely applied to restore the fertility of acidic soils by improving both physicochemical and biological properties.

title: A Cross-Sectional Study on the Presence of Mamelons in Northeastern India
creator: Anamika Nath, Saindhya Sonowal, Pawan Kumar, Ispita Das
description: IntroductionDental anthropology plays a pivotal role in human evolution and forensic sciences. This study explores a unique method for age estimation-analyzing mamelons on incisors. Mamelons are small projections on the incisal edge of permanent incisors, exhibiting age-related changes. This departure from conventional methods presents an innovative and potentially efficient approach to age estimation.

title: Survival analysis of small cell carcinoma of the esophagus: a 15-year retrospective study from a high-incidence region
creator: Wei Zhang, Jie Yuan, Baihua Yang, Jiezhong Wang, Mingqiu Chen
description: BackgroundSmall cell carcinoma of the esophagus (SCCE) is a rare malignant carcinoma, which is highly aggressive and prone to recurrence and metastasis. There is no standard therapeutic modality for SCCE. We aimed to describe the clinical characteristics and therapeutic outcomes of SCCE, analyse its prognostic factors, and provide a reference for establishing a standard treatment regimen.

title: Metformin reshapes the tumor microenvironment and enhances prognosis in invasive pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma with diabetes mellitus
creator: Rei Takahashi, Akira Saito, Hideyo Miyato, Yuki Kimura, Yuichi Aoki, Masanobu Taguchi, Kazue Morishima, Hideyuki Ohzawa, Kazuhiro Endo, Hideki Sasanuma, Hironori Yamaguchi, Hiroshi Kawahira, Hisanaga Horie, Yoshinori Hosoya, Toshiki Mimura, Joji Kitayama, Naohiro Sata
description: BackgroundPancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is frequently associated with diabetes mellitus (DM), and their prognosis remains particularly poor. Metformin, a widely used antidiabetic agent, has demonstrated anti-tumor effects through multiple mechanisms and has been associated with improved outcomes in various malignancies.

title: Nitrous Oxide Causing Subacute Combined Degeneration: A Case Report
creator: Nevin Thomas, Ravi Patel, Babaniji Oluwadamilola
description: This case report describes a 31-year-old male who developed subacute combined degeneration as a result of vitamin B12 deficiency caused by recreational use of nitrous oxide ("whippets") over a six-month period. nitrous oxide, widely available and often used for its euphoric effects, can lead to alterations in B12 metabolism and decreased myelination, particularly in the dorsal columns, with prolonged use.

title: From conservation scores to language models: a feature engineering perspective on machine learning for genetic variant interpretation
creator: Matteo Bulloni, Martina Vescio, Federico De Mori Bajolin, Linda Pattini
description: The interpretation of genetic variants remains central to precision medicine, and machine-learning-based variant effect prediction tools have become indispensable for supporting decision-making processes. In this review we trace the progression from hand-crafted features and traditional machine learning classifiers, through supervised ensembles, to deep-learning architectures and foundation models that learn representations directly from biological sequences.

title: Presumed hepatic pseudolipoma detected as a small hepatic surface lesion: multimodality imaging findings
creator: Koichi Soga, Ou Takagi, Kohei Inaba, Mikako Masuda, Ikuhiro Kobori, Katsutoshi Sugimoto
description: Hepatic pseudolipomas are uncommon benign lesions located on or near the liver capsule which are thought to arise from a detached epiploic appendage that becomes trapped near Glisson’s capsule. Because these lesions may appear as small hepatic or perihepatic nodules, they can mimic primary or metastatic hepatic tumors on screening imaging.

title: Iris Avulsion During Corneal Wound Hydration After Uneventful Cataract Extraction
creator: Lampros Lamprogiannis, Padmanabha P Syam, Arsh Patel, Kaushal Pillai Syam, George Voyatzis
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). We report a case of spontaneous total iris avulsion that occurred during corneal wound hydration following an uneventful phacoemulsification procedure. An 86-year-old woman underwent cataract surgery on her right eye, during which a single-piece acrylic intraocular lens (Bausch and Lomb Akreos Adapt Advanced Optics, Bausch and Lomb Incorporated, Rochester, NY, USA) was implanted in the bag, and the viscoelastic material was removed.

title: Understanding plant-microorganism interactions: The key roles of soil, rhizosphere, and direct and indirect mechanisms
creator: Mohamed Hnini, Karim Rabeh, Malika Oubohssaine
description: Soil, the Earth's upper crust layer, is crucial for ecological processes, comprising mineral, organic, and biological components that determine fertility and multifuncionality. Human-induced degradation necessitates advancements in pedology and soil conservation. The rhizosphere, surrounding plant roots, houses a diverse microbial community, notably bacteria, which enhance plant growth and disease resistance.

title: Long-term lactate ingestion and exercise training differentially modulate body composition, resting substrate metabolism, and tissue-specific metabolic remodeling in mice
creator: Inkwon Jang, Nayeon Kim, Deunsol Hwang, Sunghwan Kyun, Taeho Kim, Jungyong Lee, Hun-Young Park, Kiwon Lim, Jisu Kim
description: [Purpose] This study investigated whether long-term lactate ingestion induces systemic and tissue-specific metabolic adaptations under normal physiological conditions and whether these responses differ from those induced by exercise training.[Methods] Thirty-two male mice were randomly assigned to saline control, lactate ingestion, exercise training with saline, or exercise training with lactate groups (n = 8/group).

title: Marital status and competing risks of mortality in non-small cell lung cancer: a SEER-based nomogram analysis
creator: Ziqiang Wang, Tian Lan, Yangyang Xie, Ouou Yang, Congru Zhu, Zujian Hu, Jiawei He
description: BackgroundNon-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is a leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide. Beyond clinical prognostic factors, psychosocial determinants such as marital status may influence outcomes. However, its impact on cancer-specific death (CSD) and other-cause death (OCD) within a competing risk framework remains unclear.

title: A Rare Case of Tissierella praeacuta Bacteremia in the Context of Lower Extremity Cellulitis
creator: Gopal Kumar, Sahar Iqbal, Fnu Raja, Thessicar Antoine-Reid
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Tissierella praeacuta (T. praeacuta)is a gram-variable obligate anaerobe. In this case report, we describe the first documented case of T. praeacuta bacteremia in a patient with sepsis resulting from lower extremity cellulitis without concomitant osteomyelitis. During the inpatient course, the patient was treated with IV vancomycin, cefepime, and ertapenem, in addition to surgical debridement and incision and drainage of his foot wound. The patient was discharged to a skilled care nursing facility on ertapenem with significant clinical improvement.

title: Associations of adiposity and physical fitness with hippocampaldependent mnemonic discrimination in postmenopausal women
creator: Chanwoo Lee, Subin Park, Cheonok Lee, Dohyeon Lee, Hunyoung Ha, Heehyun Shin, Taeyeon Kim, Chaeeun Cho, Kyeongho Byun, Sewon Lee
description: [Purpose] This study examined the associations of adiposity indices and physical fitness components with domain-specific cognitive function in postmenopausal women, focusing on hippocampus-dependent mnemonic discrimination.[Methods] The study involved 68 postmenopausal women aged ≥ 40 years who were at least one year postmenopausal.

title: Viscoelastic Hemostatic Assays in the Management of Trauma-Induced Coagulopathy: A Clinical Update
creator: Daniele Natalini, Rikardo Xhemalaj, Simone Carelli
description: The recognition of trauma-induced coagulopathy (TIC) as an endogenous response to traumatic injuries rather than a consequence of therapeutic interventions has shifted the clinical approach toward an early and physiologically based hemostatic resuscitation. Prompt identification and correction of fibrinolysis and fibrinogen level derangements, dysregulated thrombin generation, and platelet dysfunction represent the cornerstones of the treatment strategies.

title: The effects of blood flow restriction training during low intensity online resistance training with older adults
creator: Daniela Presta, Emma H. Chen, Kate Kraemer, Andreas Bergdahl
description: [Purpose] Blood flow restriction (BFR) training involves limiting blood flow to specific areas, enabling low-intensity exercise to mimic high-intensity workouts. This study explored the effectiveness of combining BFR with online exercise classes to improve strength and functionality in older adults.

title: Erdheim-Chester Disease: A Case Report Exploring Multisystemic Involvement
creator: Francisco Antunes, Rúben Maia, Sara Henriques, Ana Ribeiro, Francisca Guimarães
description: Erdheim-Chester disease (ECD) is a rare, multisystemic, non-Langerhans cell histiocytic neoplasm predominantly affecting middle-aged males in their fifth to seventh decades of life. It often presents with nonspecific symptoms, leading to a delay in its diagnosis. We report a case of an 85-year-old male with multisystemic manifestations, including retroperitoneal, skeletal, vascular, cardiac, orbital, and central nervous system (CNS) involvement.

title: Seizing the Teachable Moment: A Pilot Study of Preventive Lifestyle Education in the Emergency Department
creator: Daniel C Keyes, Dylan L Arroyo, Ghadah W Abdulshafi, Batoul Dabajeh, Joshua Polgar, Rima Sakr, Sakibur Hasan
description: BackgroundPreventive measures are critical in avoiding and limiting the severity of diseases. Key lifestyle behaviors include sleep hygiene, habitual exercise, a healthy diet, and avoidance of risky substances, particularly the use of tobacco. The transtheoretical model (TTM) of change suggests that patients can move towards healthful changes through education.

title: Acute Coronary Syndromes: State-of-the-Art Diagnosis, Management, and Secondary Prevention
creator: Xun Yuan, Stephan Nienaber, Ibrahim Akin, Tito Kabir, Christoph A. Nienaber
description: Background: Acute coronary syndromes (ACSs) remain a leading cause of death and disability. Since the publication of the 2023 ESC ACS guidelines, multiple studies and an ESC/EAS dyslipidaemia update have refined how clinicians diagnose, revascularize, and treat ACS across the care continuum. Content: This state-of-the-art review synthesizes advances from 2023 to 2025 across five domains.

title: Successful Management of Severe and Refractory Autoimmune Hemolytic Anemia (AIHA) in a Sickle Cell Disease Patient With Bortezomib
creator: Mohammed A Alanssari, Elaf Al-Sulaitti, Zainab Al-Sulaitti, Asaad A Khalaf, Qutaiba M Dawood
description: Autoimmune hemolytic anemia (AIHA) is a multifactorial disease that causes immune-mediated red blood cell destruction, resulting in anemia and hemolysis symptoms. Despite a significant understanding of its pathogenesis, the precise causes of AIHA remain largely unclear and are thought to be multifactorial.

title: Glucosinolate–Myrosinase Formulations for Adult Obesity: Towards Next Generation of Bioactive Therapies
creator: Concepción Medrano-Padial, Cassidy Bo Harris, Verónica Mellado-Romero, Raúl Domínguez-Perles, Diego A. Moreno
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). The rising global prevalence of obesity and metabolic disorders calls for innovative dietary strategies that can modulate key enzymatic pathways involved in lipid and carbohydrate metabolism. This study uncovers the effects of sulforaphane (SFN)-rich broccoli-derived formulations—including liquid and lyophilised forms, as well as two commercial prototypes, Sulforaphan® BASIC and Sulforaphan® SMART, the latter being characterised by the inclusion of an enteric-coated myrosinase enzyme designed to enhance the in situ conversion of glucosinolates (GSL) into bioactive isothiocyanates (ITC)—on lipid and carbohydrate metabolism in

title: Seroprevalence and risk factors of infectious bovine rhinotracheitis in cattle in Gharbia governorate, Egypt: A comparative study of traditional and commercial production systems
creator: Mostafa El-Sayed El-Sheikh, Lotfy Bakar, Mamdouh Fahmy El-Mekawy, Mohammed Ibrahim Eisa, Nasser Zeidan Abouzeid, Mervat Ibrahim Abdelmonim, Sarah Gamal Yousef
description: Background:Infectious bovine rhinotracheitis (IBR) is a global contagious respiratory disease of ruminants caused by Bovine Herpes virus-1 (BoHV-1). It causes substantial financial losses in the dairy industry worldwide and is considered one of the most important causative agents of abortion and reproductive problems in dairy cattle.

title: Risk of Atrial Fibrillation Recurrence After Modified Cox-Maze IV Surgery: Comparing Atrial Functional Mitral Regurgitation and Rheumatic Mitral Regurgitation
creator: Ke Xu, Jingcheng Wu, Yi Li, Lailong Sun, Ming Yan, Fuwei Zhang, Chaobing Liu, SongLin Zhang
description: Background:The comparative efficacy of the modified Cox-Maze IV procedure (CMP IV) in treating atrial fibrillation (AF) in patients with atrial functional mitral regurgitation (AFMR) and those with rheumatic mitral regurgitation (RMR) remains inadequately characterized. Therefore, this study aimed to evaluate and compare postoperative AF recurrence rates and clinical outcomes between these two etiologically distinct groups.

title: Pathological, hematological, and biochemical alteration in broiler chickens infected with mycotoxin in Babylon province
creator: Hayder Abd AL-Emier Almremdhy, Ghusoon Abdul Kareem Neamha, Zina Bakir Al-Hilli, Rafal Jalil Awadh
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Background:Mycotoxins are considered one of the most important problems and threats that face poultry producers.Aim:This study was conducted to investigate the pathological, hematological, and biochemical alterations in chickens fed on mycotoxins contamination ration.Methods:434 feed samples were collected from poultry farms operating in Babil Governorate/Iraq, where feed samples were collected over the course of 2023, and these samples were tested by direct competitive enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay to determine the level of mycotoxins.

title: A retrospective description of blood and urine alterations in 386 male cats with urethral obstruction in Botucatu, São Paulo, Brazil
creator: Reiner Silveira de Moraes, Diego Ribeiro, Alessandra Melchert, Henry David Mogollón García, Doughlas Regalin, Raphael Lú cio Andreatti Filho, Regina Kiomi Takahira, Rogério Giuffrida, Adriano Sakai Okamoto, Priscylla Tatiana Chalfun Guimarães-Okamoto
description: Background:Urinary retention in obstructed male cats leads to changes in blood and urine compounds, which, combined with the time of obstruction, are linked to the worsening of the animal’s clinical status.Aim:This study aimed to describe the primary laboratory changes in male cats with urethral obstruction (UO).

title: Skirted Prosthetic Valves Are Associated With Increased Risk of Subclinical Leaflet Thrombosis Following Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement: A Multicenter Study
creator: Yifan Yang, Qiang Li, Jing Yao, Yunfeng Yan, Moyang Wang, Xinmin Liu, Fei Yuan, Zhengming Jiang, Taiyang Luo, Qian Zhang, Yongjian Wu, Guangyuan Song
description: Background:Subclinical leaflet thrombosis (SLT) is associated with an increased risk of thromboembolic events, valve dysfunction, and mortality in patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). However, data on the incidence and risk factors for SLT in patients undergoing TAVR using self-expanding valves (SEVs) remain limited.

title: Detection of the methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus gene encoding mecA in nasal swabs of cats in Surabaya, Indonesia
creator: Safira Ramadhani, Aswin Rafif Khairullah, Mustofa Helmi Effendi, Mohammad Sukmanadi, Wiwiek Tyasningsih, Saumi Kirey Millannia, Daniah Ashri Afnani, Ikechukwu Benjamin Moses, M Thoriq Ihza Farizqi, Sergius Erikson Kaben
description: Background:The most susceptible group of people to spread methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) among domestic cats is their owners’ relatives.Aim:Considering the aforementioned, research at the Surabaya City Animal Hospital is necessary to determine whether the mecA gene may be detected in cat nasal swabs.Methods:Samples were taken using a sterile cotton swab, and the transport medium was buffered peptone water.

title: Effect of nano curcumin administration on IL-6 expression in placental organs and fetal weight exposed to stress during pregnancy in mice
creator: Viski Fitri Hendrawan, Yudit Oktanella, Habib Syaiful Arif Tuska, Intan Firdha Olien Noor Al Ichsan
description: Background:Stress can cause an increase in proinflammatory cytokines, IL-6, which plays a role in the inflammatory response and causes changes in the placenta, causing a low risk of the fetus being born. Giving nanocurcumin, which functions as an anti-inflammatory and antioxidant, is expected to reduce cortisol levels which increase during pregnancy.

title: Predictive Value of the Systemic Immune-Inflammation Index for Cardiovascular Events in Patients With Chronic Total Coronary Occlusion
creator: Yuhao Zhao, Ping Wang, Shun Zhao, Qin Ma, Ze Zheng, Yuchen Shi, Jinghua Liu
description: Background:This large-scale cohort study aimed to evaluate the prognostic role of the systemic immune-inflammation index (SII) in patients with chronic total occlusion (CTO) undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI).Methods:A total of 3107 patients with CTO lesions who underwent PCI were enrolled in this study.

title: Fatigue Life Assessment of Notched PLA Manufactured Using FDM 3D-Printing Technique
creator: Mahsima Seifollahi, Mohammad Zaman Kabir
description: Fused Deposition Modeling (FDM) is an extensively employed additive manufacturing method for producing precise and complicated polymer models, with its industrial applications expanding under various loading conditions. A review of existing research highlights the insufficient investigation of the influence of geometric discontinuities in additively manufactured polylactic acid (PLA) members under fatigue loads.

title: Bovine trichomoniasis: A hidden threat to reproductive efficiency
creator: Herry Agoes Hermadi, Aswin Rafif Khairullah, Yenny Damayanti, Erma Safitri, Wiwiek Tyasningsih, Sunaryo Hadi Warsito, Kartika Afrida Fauzia, Bantari Wisynu Kusuma Wardhani, Fitrine Ekawasti, Syahputra Wibowo, Ima Fauziah, Ikechukwu Benjamin Moses, Dea Anita Ariani Kurniasih, Muhammad Khaliim Jati Ku
description: Bovine trichomoniasis is a reproductive illness that affects cattle causing pyometra, early to mid-pregnancy miscarriages, and lower birth rates. Tritrichomonas foetus is a flagellated protozoan which first discovered in France in 1888 and composts three phases during its lifecycle including trophozoite, cyst, and pseudocyst.

title: Dual-Band, Dual-Mode, Circularly Polarized Fully Woven Textile Antenna for Simultaneous Wireless Information and Power Transfer in Wearable Applications
creator: Miguel Fernández, Carlos Vázquez, Samuel Ver Hoeye
description: In this work, a dual-band, dual-mode, circularly polarized fully woven textile antenna with capability for Simultaneous Wireless Information and Power Transfer (SWIPT) in wearable applications is presented. The power and the data transfer modes work at 2.4 and 5.4 GHz, respectively. The radiating element is based on a square patch with an asymmetrical U-shaped slot and a chamfered corner.

title: Non-Ultrasound-Guided Versus Ultrasound-Guided Femoral Venous Puncture in the Interventional Pulmonary Embolism Era: Does Ultrasound Guidance Improve Safety and Feasibility?
creator: Abdelrahman Elhakim, Desouki Abdelatti, Mohamed Elhakim, Osama Bisht, Ibrahim Yassin, Mohamed A Mosaad, Ahmad M Hassaan, Peter W. Radke, Mohammed Saad
description: Background:The use of interventional endovascular therapy for pulmonary embolism (PE) has become increasingly important over the last decade. In contrast to other cardiovascular interventions, these procedures carry a higher risk of access-related bleeding due to the acute clinical setting, elevated body mass index, and the frequent need for high-dose anticoagulation.

title: Molecular docking of eleven snake venom peptides targeting human immunodeficiency virus capsid glycoprotein as inhibitors
creator: Mousa O Germoush, Maged Fouda, Mohammad J S Mantargi, Moustafa Sarhan, Barakat M Alrashdi, Diaa Massoud, Sarah Alzwain, Nehmat Ghaboura, Ahmed E Altyar, Mohamed M Abdel-Daim
description: Background:Snake venoms are mainly composed of a mixture of proteins and peptides with antiviral activity against several viruses including HIV. Therefore, snake venoms represent a promising source for new antiviral drugs.Aim:The study examines the toxin’s capacity to disrupt the spike glycoprotein of HIV, the virus accountable for the HIV epidemic.

title: Phylodynamic analysis provides insights into genotype displacement of duck hepatitis A virus in China
creator: Chenyi Xie, Baoyan Wang, Ying Wang, Guangrong Zhao, Yang Liu, Jianlong Zhang, Xin Yu, Linlin Jiang, Jiayu Yu, Jiuyu Zhan, Hongwei Zhu, Xingxiao Zhang
description: ImportanceDuck viral hepatitis, caused by the duck hepatitis A virus (DHAV), poses a significant threat to the global duck industry, particularly in China.ObjectiveThis study examined the evolutionary mechanisms driving the genotype displacement of DHAV-1 by DHAV-3 in China using phylodynamic analysis.

title: Adaptive Localization-Free Secure Routing Protocol for Underwater Sensor Networks
creator: Ayman Alharbi, Saleh Ibrahim
description: Depth-based probabilistic routing (DPR) is an efficient underwater acoustic network (UAN) routing protocol which resists the depth-spoofing attack. DPR’s optimal value of the unqualified forwarding probability depends on the UAN topology, condition, and threat state, which are highly dynamic. If the static forwarding probability used in DPR is set too low for the current state, packet delivery ratio (PDR) drops.

title: New technology and emerging theories driving progress in neuropsychiatric disorders
creator: Zengliang Jin
description: characterized by complex pathogenesis and high heterogeneity, and currently, effective and universal treatments for most neuropsychiatric disorders remain scarce [2]. Fortunately, recent technological advancements, grounded in emerging scientific theories, have paved the way for novel theraputic approaches. Genetic technologies, particularly single-cell genomics, hold promise for uncovering the regulatory mechanisms underlying brain-related traits.

title: Isolation and Characterization of Bioactive Compounds from Saccharomonospora sp. CMS18 and Their Antifungal Properties
creator: Soohyun Um, Hyeongju Jeong, Ji-Eun Park, Jeongwon Seo, Sang Heon Jung, Munhyung Bae, Kyung-Tae Lee, Kyuho Moon, Mostafa Rateb
description: In this study, metagenomic analysis was employed to investigate the bacterial communities in the Muan tidal mudflat of the Republic of Korea. We used metagenomic analysis to identify the microbial community in tidal soil dominated by Proteobacteria. From this environment, the bacterial strain, Saccharomonospora sp. CMS18, was isolated and yielded two previously unknown compounds, penipaline D (3) and N-acetyl-dimethylallyltryptophan (4).

title: Recommendations for Adult Pneumococcal Vaccination in Korea: 2026 Update Incorporating the 21-Valent Pneumococcal Conjugate Vaccine
creator: Joon Young Song, Ki Tae Kwon, Wan Beom Park, Ji Yun Noh, Sun Hee Park, Eun Ju Choo, Min Joo Choi, Jun Yong Choi, Jung Yeon Heo, Won Suk Choi, the Committee of Adult Immunization in the Korean Society of Infectious Diseases
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The 21-valent pneumococcal conjugate vaccine (PCV21; CAPVAXIVE; Merck Sharp & Dohme) is the first pneumococcal conjugate vaccine (PCV) specifically designed for adults, targeting serotypes that currently cause disease in this population. PCV21 includes 11 serotypes not contained in any other approved PCV (9N, 15A, 15C, 16F, 17F, 20A, 23A, 23B, 24F, 31, and 35B), together with serotypes 3, 6A, 7F, 8, 10A, 11A, 12F, 19A, 22F, and 33F.

title: Late HIV Presentation Remains High in Korea: 28-Year National Surveillance Trends and the Limits of Inference under Incomplete CD4 Capture, 1998–2025
creator: EunKyung Nam, Shin-Woo Kim, Sohyun Bae, Yoonjung Kim
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundWhether late human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) presentation in Korea has improved is difficult to judge because a CD4 count at diagnosis was captured for only a minority of notified cases until 2025.

title: Robust Learning-Based Detection with Cost Control and Byzantine Mitigation
creator: Chen Zhong, M. Cenk Gursoy, Senem Velipasalar
description: To address the state estimation and detection problem in the presence of noisy sensor observations, probing costs, and communication noise, we in this paper propose a soft actor-critic (SAC) deep reinforcement learning (DRL) framework for dynamically scheduling sensors and sequentially probing the state of a stochastic system.

title: RETRACTED: Atta et al. Functionalization of Magnetite Nanoparticles as Oil Spill Collector. Int. J. Mol. Sci. 2015, 16, 6911–6931
creator: Ayman M. Atta, Hamad A. Al-Lohedan, Sami A. Al-Hussain
description: Adhering to our standard procedure, an investigation was conducted by the Editorial Office and Editorial Board that identified indications of inappropriate editing in Figures 1, 2 and 4 and partial duplication in Figure 7B presented in this article [1], with earlier publications [2,3,4] presenting different experimental conditions.

title: Exposure to Environmental Pollutants and the Risk of Respiratory Illnesses in 36-Month-Old Children: The Korean Children’s Environmental Health Study (Ko-CHENS)
creator: Changmin Kang, Seung-Ah Choe, Hyunseo Kim, Geunhwa Lee, JungHeum Jo, Jue Seong Lee, Dae Jin Song, Young Yoo, Ko-CHENS Study group
description: PurposeThis study aimed to investigate the association of exposure to environmental pollutants and surrounding residential environments with the development of respiratory illnesses in 36-month-old children using data from the Korean CHildren’s ENvironmental health Study.MethodsDemographic information and anthropometric measurements were obtained from the newborns. At 36 months of age, indoor environmental pollutant levels (particulate matter [PM10 and PM2.

title: Extraction and Analytical Methods for the Characterization of Polyphenols in Marine Microalgae: A Review
creator: Gabriela Bermudez, Cristina Terenzi, Francesca Medri, Vincenza Andrisano, Serena Montanari, Xiaxia Di, Margarida Costa
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Marine microalgae are emerging as promising sources of polyphenols, renowned for their health-promoting benefits. Recovering polyphenols from microalgae requires suitable treatment and extraction techniques to ensure their release from the biomass and analytical methodologies to assess their efficiency. This review provides a comprehensive comparison of traditional and cutting-edge extraction and analytical procedures applied for polyphenolic characterization in marine microalgae over the past 26 years, with a unique perspective on optimizing their recovery and identification.

title: Lessons Learnt from the Belimumab Trials in Systemic Lupus Erythematosus
creator: Leonardo Palazzo, Alexander Tsoi, Dionysis Nikolopoulos, Ioannis Parodis
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Belimumab, a human monoclonal antibody that works against B-cell activating factor (BAFF), has significantly advanced the management of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). Beyond the initial Phase III randomised controlled trials (RCTs) that demonstrated efficacy for belimumab as an add-on to non-biological standard therapy (ST) along with a favourable safety profile, more than 50 post hoc analyses of RCT data have provided additional insights into its clinical utility.

title: E2F1-Activated lncRNA FTX Promotes Asthma Progression via Regulating the SRSF1/RBPJ Axis
creator: Yuting Lai, Guoqing Qiu, Na Li, Yuming Chen, Yan Shen
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). PurposeLong non-coding RNA five prime to Xist (FTX) is considered a regulator for asthma. Therefore, we aimed to explore its more roles and molecular mechanisms in asthma process.MethodsSerum samples from controls and asthmatics were collected. Asthma mouse models were induced with ovalbumin (OVA), and cell models were established using airway smooth muscle cells (ASMCs) treated with platelet-derived growth factor BB (PDGF-BB). The inspiratory and expiratory airway resistances of mice were examined by measuring airway hyperresponsiveness.

title: Enhancing Large Language Model Reliability: Minimizing Hallucinations with Dual Retrieval-Augmented Generation Based on the Latest Diabetes Guidelines
creator: Jaedong Lee, Hyosoung Cha, Yul Hwangbo, Wonjoong Cheon
description: Background/Objectives: Large language models (LLMs) show promise in healthcare but face challenges with hallucinations, particularly in rapidly evolving fields like diabetes management. Traditional LLM updating methods are resource-intensive, necessitating new approaches for delivering reliable, current medical information. This study aimed to develop and evaluate a novel retrieval system to enhance LLM reliability in diabetes management across different languages and guidelines.

title: From Symptomatic Therapies to Disease-Modifying Approaches for Neuronal Sodium Channel Disorders
creator: Giorgia Dinoi, Ileana Canfora, Daniela D’Agnano, Brigida Boccanegra, Elena Conte, Annamaria De Luca, Antonella Liantonio, Vittorio Sciruicchio, Paola Imbrici
description: Variants in neuronal sodium channel genes are responsible for a spectrum of neurological disorders, including developmental and epileptic encephalopathies (DEEs), with considerable genetic and phenotypic heterogeneity and drug resistance. Gene variants can produce loss-, gain-, or mixed-function effects, resulting in complex genotype-phenotype correlations.

title: Intraoperative ventilation settings in Germany: an observational multicentre cross-sectional study
creator: Linda Grüßer, András Keszei, Rolf Rossaint, Berit Zingraf, Julia Wallqvist, Sebastian Goldmann, Mark Coburn, Andreas Güldner, Thomas Hachenberg, Christian Hönemann, Thea Koch, Bert Mierke, Martin Schuster, Hermann Wrigge, Julia Schuler, Jan Larmann, Ana Kowark, NO-HARM Study Group, German Society of
description: PurposeIntraoperative lung protective ventilation and, in inhalational anesthesia, minimal fresh gas flow (FGF) are recommended. It remains unclear how these recommendations are transferred to clinical routine. We aimed to assess corresponding anesthesia practices in Germany and raise awareness of optimal ventilation settings.

title: Parkinson’s disease-associated LRRK2 risk variant, G2385R, enhances Rab substrate phosphorylation and impairs neuronal integrity
creator: An Phu Tran Nguyen, Roger Moser, Nicole Bryant, Lindsey A Cunningham, Evan J Worden, Darren J Moore
description: Mutations in the LRRK2 gene are the most frequent cause of familial Parkinson’s disease (PD) whereas common variants are associated with an increased risk for sporadic PD. LRRK2 encodes a multi-domain protein displaying two functional enzymatic activities: GTPase and kinase. In addition to familial mutations, several common LRRK2 coding variants have been associated with PD risk in different ethnic populations.

title: Fertility-Related Concerns in Long-Term Survivors of Childhood Cancer: A Canadian Cohort Study
creator: Pauline Holmer, Brianna Henry, Jenny Duong, Oluwaseyi A Lawal, Miranda M Fidler-Benaoudia, Kathleen Reynolds, Gisela Michel, Vicky Lehmann, Fiona S M Schulte
description: Survivors of childhood cancer face reduced fertility, which can be a significant cause for concern. Our study aimed to assess the prevalence of fertility-related concerns and identify associated factors. Self-report data were collected with the Long-Term Survivor Questionnaire at the Alberta Children’s Hospital’s Long-Term Survivor Clinic (LTSC) between January 2021 and September 2023.

title: Soil microbial responses to long-term agricultural practices under no-till: insights from depth-resolved sampling of shallow soil layers
creator: Melina Soledad Piacenza, Silvina Bacigaluppo, Mariana Maury, Fernando Salvagiotti, Frank Guzman, Esteban G Jobbágy, Valeria S Faggioli
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Fungal and bacterial communities were characterized at three soil depths (0–3.5 cm, 3.5–7.5 cm, and 7.5–15 cm) in a 15-year no-till field experiment involving diversified crop rotations with two levels of nitrogen fertilization and soybean monoculture. We hypothesized that community patterns associated with agricultural practices would be most evident in the uppermost soil layer, and that potentially plant-pathogenic taxa would be more abundant under soybean monoculture. Bacterial community composition varied with soil depth but not among agricultural practices.

title: Mechano-regulation of germline development, maintenance, and differentiation
creator: Ishani Sharma, Anup Padmanabhan
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Highlights•Germline development and functioning is regulated by mechanical stimuli.•Cell intrinsic and extrinsic factors govern germline development and maintenance.•Germline mechano-regulation is generally conserved across organisms.Keywords: Germline, Mechano-transduction, Cytoskeleton, Mechanics, Cell adhesion, Cell fate Introduction By virtue of its ability to transmit genetic information accurately to the next generation, the germline ensures the perpetuation of a species and is therefore subjected to rigorous scrutiny. It comprises mature gametes and stem/progenitor cells at various stages of development.

title: Clinical, Genetic, and Immunological Spectrum of CHAI and LATAIE Patients from a Tertiary Referral Centre in India
creator: Priyanka Setia, Umair Ahmed Bargir, Mukesh Desai, Aparna Dalvi, Shweta Shinde, Neha Jodhawat, Pallavi Gaikwad, Sagar Bhattad, Chandrakala Shainmukhaih, Maya Gupta, Amruta Dhawale, Priyanka Kambli, Reetika Malik Yadav, Manas Kalra, Harikrishnan Gangadharan, Meena Sivasankaran, Vibha Bafna, Prawin Kum
description: Primary immune regulatory disorders (PIRDs) are a group of conditions characterised by a loss of immune tolerance. Two such disorders, CHAI and LATAIE, share common molecular mechanisms, leading to significant clinical overlap. Here, we report demographic, clinical, immunological, and molecular findings in 29 patients referred from different parts of India with a diagnosis of CHAI or LATAIE.

title: Mechanism of NanR transcriptional activation of sialic acid metabolism in Streptococcus pneumoniae
creator: David M Wood, Ashleigh S Johns, Zachary D Tillett, Heather L Shearer, Santosh Panjikar, Yee-Foong Mok, Michael D W Griffin, Timothy M Allison, Rachel A North, Paul E Pace, Borries Demeler, Mark B Hampton, Renwick C J Dobson, Christopher R Horne
description: In Streptococcus pneumoniae, the RpiR transcriptional regulator NanR (SpNanR) senses sialic acid in the environment and upregulates transcription of the nan and sia A operons to increase uptake and metabolism of sialic acid. The molecular basis of this activation is unknown. Here, we demonstrate that SpNanR binds N-acetylmannosamine-6-phosphate, a metabolite of sialic acid catabolism.

title: Exploring the therapeutic potential of triterpenoid saponins from Gymnema sylvestre: Mechanistic insights into hepatoprotection, immunomodulation, anticancer activities, molecular docking, and pharmacokinetics
creator: Vasudeva Reddy Netala, Tianyu Hou, Rajakumari Devarapogu, Murali Satyanarayana Bethu, Zhijun Zhang, Tartte Vijaya
description: The study comprehensively investigated the therapeutic potential of Gymnema sylvestre triterpenoid saponin extract (GST), encompassing its hepatoprotective, immunomodulatory, and anticancer activities. The study employed a Prednisolone (PRD)-induced immunosuppressed rat model to assess the hepatoprotective and immunomodulatory effects of GST. Using this model, GST was found to modulate haematopoiesis, improving RBC, platelet, and WBC counts, underscoring its potential in hematopoietic homeostasis.

title: Donor- and Acceptor-Side Protection Against Photosystem I Photoinhibition in Arabidopsis thaliana
creator: Marina Kozuleva
description: Photosystem I (PSI) photoinhibition (PI(I)) is gaining traction as a potentially more significant threat to plant performance than photoinhibition of photosystem II (PSII). The increased focus is facilitated by the implementation of specific protocols that induce PI(I), such as artificial fluctuating light (FL) and repetitive short saturating pulses (rSPs). rSPs were long considered a specific sub-case of FL.

title: Treatable traits-based management of bronchiectasis: moving from theory to clinical practice
creator: Guiyin Zhu, James D. Chalmers, Jin-Fu Xu
description: Bronchiectasis is a chronic airway disease characterized by irreversible bronchial dilatation and substantial clinical heterogeneity. Accumulating evidence from large international observational cohorts has highlighted wide variation in the features of this disease and unmet clinical needs. The treatable traits-based approach has emerged as a means to prioritize identifiable and clinically actionable problems over traditional diagnostic labels.

title: The concurrence of osteochondromatosis and bone infarction in a patient with anterior cruciate ligament rupture: a rare case report
creator: Tai Duc Tran, Duc Hoang Tran, Vuong Ngoc Vu, Toan Nguyen Thanh, Tri Quang Le
description: Introduction:Synovial osteochondromatosis and bone infarction are two uncommon conditions that typically present independently and are frequently misdiagnosed due to their nonspecific symptoms. This case highlights an exceptionally rare clinical scenario, underscoring the importance of meticulous imaging evaluation and integrated surgical management.

title: Neural Network-Enabled Process Flowsheet for Industrial Shot Peening
creator: Langdon Feltner, Paul Mort
description: This work presents a dynamic flowsheet model that predicts residual stress from shot peening. The peening medium is characterized by size and shape, and evolves dynamically with abrasion, fracture, classification, and replenishment. Because particle size and impact location vary stochastically, the resulting residual stress field is spatially heterogeneous.

title: Optimising a digital parent-based intervention to improve adolescent health risk behaviours in families living in socio-economically disadvantaged communities: findings from the Health4Life Parents & Teens factorial randomised trial
creator: Katrina E Champion, Lily Davidson, Matthew Sunderland, Emily Hunter, Bonnie Spring, Louise Thornton, Alex Haidinger, Tara Finn, Bridie Osman, Cath Chapman, Tracy Burrows, Tim Slade, Stephanie R Partridge, Lauren A Gardner, Belinda J Parmenter, Louise A Baur, Maree Teesson, Cathrine Mihalopoulos, Geo
description: SummaryBackgroundAdolescence is a critical period when health risk behaviours contributing to long-term disease burden emerge. Parent-based interventions show promise, yet engagement is often low and few exist for socioeconomically disadvantaged communities. We applied the Multiphase Optimisation Strategy (MOST) to identify a maximally effective, minimally burdensome digital intervention to support parents to improve adolescent health risk behaviours.

title: Elucidating metabolic pathways through genomic analysis in highly heavy metal-resistant Halobacterium salinarum strains
creator: Houda Baati, Mariem Siala, Souad Benali, Chafai Azri, Christopher Dunlap, Rosa María Martínez-Espinosa, Mohamed Trigui
description: The annotated and predicted genomes of five archaeal strains (AS1, AS2, AS8, AS11 and AS19), isolated from Sfax solar saltern sediments (Tunisia) and affiliated with Halobacterium salinarum, were performed by RAST webserver (Rapid Annotation using Subsystem Technology) and NCBI prokaryotic genome annotation pipeline (PGAP).

title: Assessment of the Diagnostic Value of [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-04 and [18F]FDG PET in a PHMG-p-Induced Pulmonary Fibrosis Murine Model
creator: So Young Kim, Jun Young Park, Ye Lim Cho, Won Jun Kang
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Background/Objectives: Pulmonary fibrosis is a progressive and fatal lung disease with limited diagnostic and therapeutic options. Fibroblast activation protein (FAP) has emerged as a promising molecular imaging target for the non-invasive assessment of fibrotic activity. This study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic feasibility of [68Ga]Ga-FAP inhibitor (FAPI) and [18F]fluorodeoxyglucose ([18F]FDG) positron emission tomography (PET) for imaging pulmonary fibrosis in a mouse model. Methods: A pulmonary fibrosis model was established by intratracheal administration of polyhexamethylene guanidine-phosphate (PHMG-p) to C57BL/6 mice.

title: Determination of optimum probiotic dosage for the culture of whiteleg shrimp, Litopenaeus vannamei in an indoor system
creator: Edward Terhemen Akange, Benjamin Orfega Kwaghvihi, Olumide A Odeyemi, Hajar Rastegari, Muhamad Shukri Shafie, Ahmad Ideris Abdul Rahim, Amyra Suryatie Kamaruzzan, Siti Rozaimah Sheikh Abdullah, Nor Azman Kasan
description: Determining the optimum application dosage of probiotic in biofloc system is often challenging because the microbial community seems to exert similar effects irrespective of their dosages. It is however noted that certain dosages promote higher yield in shrimp culture more effectively.

title: Adoptive cell therapy in lung cancer: progress, challenges, and prospects
creator: Jingyi Li, Chan Tong, Yongchang Chen, Bo Zhu
description: Lung cancer is the leading cause of cancer-related deaths worldwide. Over the past decade, immunotherapy, represented by immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) targeting programmed cell death protein-1/programmed cell death protein ligand-1 (PD-1/PD-L1) or cytotoxic T lymphocyte associated antigen-4 (CTLA-4), has revolutionized the treatment paradigm of lung cancer, reducing the risk of death by approximately 30%.

title: Aggressive mediastinal amyloidosis mimicking malignancy: a case report
creator: Sergio Andres Siado Guerrero, Jorge Ramírez Pereira, María Paula Motta Aguirre, Yeni Alexandra Arroyave-Guerrero
description: Introduction:Amyloidosis is characterized by extracellular protein fibril deposition. Light-chain (AL) amyloidosis may be associated with plasma cell dyscrasias. Isolated mediastinal involvement is exceptionally rare and may mimic malignant tumors.Case presentation:A 69-year-old woman presented with a progressively enlarging anterior chest wall mass caused by an invasive mediastinal lesion. Biopsy revealed amyloid deposition.

title: Platelet Count Normalization Following Romosozumab Treatment for Osteoporosis in Patient with Immune Thrombocytopenic Purpura: A Case Report and Literature Review
creator: Kyunghun Sung, Jeonghoon Ha
description: Romosozumab, which is approved for the treatment of osteoporosis, has a dual-action mechanism that promotes bone formation and inhibits bone resorption. However, its association with an increased risk of major adverse cardiovascular events, as highlighted in the ARCH I study, raises concerns. The underlying pathophysiological mechanisms, possibly involving changes in platelet dynamics, are yet to be fully elucidated.

title: Polyphenols, Polysaccharides, and Their Complexes from Aronia melanocarpa in the Chemoprevention of Colorectal Cancer
creator: Karolina Niewinna, Katarzyna Owczarek, Zuzanna Senkowska, Urszula Lewandowska
description: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is among the three most commonly diagnosed malignancies worldwide and remains a major public health challenge, emphasizing the need for effective preventive strategies. Considering the current chemotherapy limitations of key agents, natural products widely researched as dietary supplements can complement conventional treatments.

title: Osteoporosis screening and management framework for community-based primary care in Hong Kong: A Delphi consensus study
creator: Ching-Lung Cheung, Hing-Sun Chan, Pak-Kin Chan, Alvina Wing-Sze Chau, Cindy Ming-Wah Choi, Dicky Ka-Chun Chow, Dilys Yan-Wing Chow, Hoi-Yan Chung, Bonnie So-Kuen Lam, Wing-Wo Lam, Bonnie Leung, Yuen-Lok Ma, Janus Chi-Keung Wong, Sze-Hung Wong, Kenny Wai-Ming Wong, William Ho-Ching Yuen
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). ObjectivesOsteoporosis poses a significant public health challenge as it leads to an increased incidence of fractures. This can result in considerable disability and substantial financial burdens. With the rapidly aging population in Hong Kong, the incidence and impact of osteoporotic fractures are expected to rise, underscoring the need for a coordinated, community-based care model to identify at-risk older adults and offer timely management.MethodsThis study adopted a Delphi methodology to develop consensus statements and a structured framework for community osteoporosis screening and management

title: Usnic acid brief exposure suppresses cariogenic properties and complexity of Streptococcus mutans biofilms
creator: Santosh Pandit, Mi-A Kim, Ji-Eun Jung, Hyeon-Mi Choi, Jae-Gyu Jeon
description: Bacterial biofilms are highly structured surface associated architecture of micro-colonies, which are strongly bonded with the exopolymeric matrix of their own synthesis. These exopolymeric substances, mainly exopolysaccharides (EPS) initially assist the bacterial adhesion and finally form a bridge over the microcolonies to protect them from environmental assaults and antimicrobial exposure.

title: Deep learning segmentation of the cerebral ventricular system and brainstem for pediatric radiotherapy planning
creator: Feline Heinzelmann, Fabian Hörst, Lukas Heine, Jana Fragemann, Moritz Rempe, Gijs Luijten, Sarah Peters, Julian Hlouschek, Jan Egger, Beate Timmermann, Jens Kleesiek, Christian Bäumer
description: Background and PurposeSegmentation of the cerebral ventricular system (VS) is central to radiotherapy, both for whole-ventricular irradiation in intracranial germ cell tumors (GCTs) and protection of the periventricular region. Complex, variable VS anatomy makes manual delineation challenging and hampers auto-segmentation model development.

title: Quasi-Newton optimised Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks for wind farm power prediction
creator: Auwalu Saleh Mubarak, Zubaida Said Ameen, Sagiru Mati, Ayodele Lasisi, Quadri Noorulhasan Naveed, Rabiu Aliyu Abdulkadir
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Having accurate and effective wind energy forecasting that can be easily incorporated into smart networks is important. Appropriate planning and energy generation predictions are necessary for these infrastructures. The production of wind energy is linked to instability and unpredictability. Wind energy forecasting has traditionally been performed using statistical models, but with the advent of artificial intelligence (AI), research indicates that AI is more accurate than the statical technique.

title: Genital self-image and sexual distress in married women with and without sexual intimate partner violence experience in Iran
creator: Maryam Farjamfar, Zeinab Hamzehgardeshi, Afsaneh Keramat, Masoud Yunesian, Mina Malary
description: ObjectivesThe impact of sexual intimate partner violence (SIPV) on female genital self-image and sexual distress is not well understood. We aimed to assess whether women with and without SIPV experiences differed in terms ofgenital self-image and sexual distress.MethodsAn online survey was conducted among married, reproductive-age women registered at healthcare centers in Amol, northern Iran.

title: From descriptive to generative: foundation-model approaches for spatial transcriptomics
creator: Ting Fan, Yufei Leng, Jiatong Zhang, Zhichang Zhang
description: Spatial transcriptomics has advanced the study of biological systems by facilitating the mapping of gene expression within native tissue environments. Nevertheless, the intrinsic high dimensionality, pronounced data sparsity, and intricate nonlinear relationships between tissue morphology and the transcriptome pose challenges for conventional analytical frameworks in capturing long-range biological dependencies.

title: Conception rate according to the size and location of corpus luteum and coexistent follicle before embryo transfer in Hanwoo
creator: Su-Geun Lim, Junkoo Yi, Jaejung Ha, Jinyeon Park, Woo-Sung Kwon, Daejung Yu, Zaeyoung Ryoo, Daehyun Kim
description: The size and location of the corpus luteum and the presence of coexistent follicles are crucial factors in synchronizing recipients and determining the suitability for embryo transfer. However, there has been a recent decline in conception rates after embryo transfer, which is attributed to environmental pollution, uterine inflammation, ovarian cysts, and other factors.

title: HESTIA: scalable multimodal integration of histology and high-resolution spatial Transcriptomics for robust spatial domain identification
creator: Zheng Zhong, Xiaoyu Zhu, Jing Guo, Sha Liao, Ao Chen
description: Spatial omics has revolutionized molecular biology by providing invaluable insights into how native tissue microenvironments regulate cellular functions and disease mechanisms. Accurately capturing this structural complexity and decoding the underlying biological processes requires effectively integrating data from multiple modalities. However, transitioning to subcellular resolutions introduces massive data scales and severe transcriptomic sparsity, which challenge current analytical frameworks.

title: Olive Leaf Extract (OLE) Anti-Tumor Activities Against Hematologic Tumors: Potential Therapeutic Implications for Pediatric Patients with B-Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia
creator: Irma Airoldi, Lucrezia Canè, Chiara Brignole, Eleonora Ciampi, Daniela Montagna, Fabio Morandi
description: Background/Objectives: Several studies reported that olive leaf extract (OLE) may exert potent anti-cancer activities against human solid and hematological tumors. Such effects are mostly related to the polyphenol oleuropein and its derivatives, which are highly concentrated in OLE. Here, we investigated the anti-tumor effects of OLE in vitro against human acute leukemia and lymphoma cells.

title: Effect of crating density and weather conditions during transit on preslaughter losses, physiological characteristics, and meat quality in broilers
creator: Myunghwan Yu, Elijah Ogola Oketch, Nuwan Chamara Chathuranga, Shan Randima Nawarathne, Jun Seon Hong, Venuste Maniraguha, Bernadette G Sta Cruz, Eunsoo Seo, Jeseok Lee, Haeeun Park, Jung Min Heo
description: The impact of crating density and prevailing weather conditions during transit on preslaughter losses, physiological characteristics, and meat quality in broilers was investigated.
